---- MODULE W4Od0m6p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Teams, ORs, Instances, LeaseLen, NoTeam, NoInst

\* A hospital operating-room scheduler: surgical teams request time in one of
\* a small shared pool of operating rooms. Two independent scheduler
\* instances (e.g. two wings' coordination processes) both grant leases out
\* of the very same pool of rooms, so correctness cannot rely on either
\* instance alone -- both must respect the same shared grant record. A
\* granted lease automatically ages every tick and is force-expired once it
\* reaches LeaseLen, or it can be released voluntarily by its team.
\* The invariant protects mutual exclusion: a room is never actively leased
\* to two different teams at the same time, no matter which instance granted it.

VARIABLES grants, grantInst, leaseAge, requesting

TypeOK ==
  /\ grants \subseteq (ORs \times Teams)
  /\ grantInst \in [ORs -> Instances \cup {NoInst}]
  /\ leaseAge \in [ORs -> 0..LeaseLen]
  /\ requesting \subseteq Teams

Init ==
  /\ grants = {}
  /\ grantInst = [o \in ORs |-> NoInst]
  /\ leaseAge = [o \in ORs |-> 0]
  /\ requesting = {}

RoomFree(o) == \A t \in Teams : <<o, t>> \notin grants
HasGrant(t)  == \E o \in ORs : <<o, t>> \in grants

Request(t) ==
  /\ t \notin requesting
  /\ ~HasGrant(t)
  /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, grantInst, leaseAge>>

Grant(o, t, i) ==
  /\ t \in requesting
  /\ RoomFree(o)
  /\ grants' = grants \cup {<<o, t>>}
  /\ grantInst' = [grantInst EXCEPT ![o] = i]
  /\ leaseAge' = [leaseAge EXCEPT ![o] = 0]
  /\ requesting' = requesting \ {t}

Tick(o) ==
  /\ ~RoomFree(o)
  /\ leaseAge[o] < LeaseLen
  /\ leaseAge' = [leaseAge EXCEPT ![o] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, grantInst, requesting>>

Expire(o) ==
  /\ \E t \in Teams : <<o, t>> \in grants
  /\ leaseAge[o] >= LeaseLen
  /\ grants' = {p \in grants : p[1] # o}
  /\ grantInst' = [grantInst EXCEPT ![o] = NoInst]
  /\ leaseAge' = [leaseAge EXCEPT ![o] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED requesting

Release(o) ==
  /\ ~RoomFree(o)
  /\ leaseAge[o] < LeaseLen
  /\ grants' = {p \in grants : p[1] # o}
  /\ grantInst' = [grantInst EXCEPT ![o] = NoInst]
  /\ leaseAge' = [leaseAge EXCEPT ![o] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED requesting

GrantFor(t) == \E o \in ORs, i \in Instances : Grant(o, t, i)
TickAny      == \E o \in ORs : Tick(o)
ExpireAny    == \E o \in ORs : Expire(o)

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Teams : Request(t)
  \/ \E o \in ORs, t \in Teams, i \in Instances : Grant(o, t, i)
  \/ TickAny
  \/ ExpireAny
  \/ \E o \in ORs : Release(o)

vars == <<grants, grantInst, leaseAge, requesting>>

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A t \in Teams : SF_vars(GrantFor(t))
  /\ WF_vars(TickAny)
  /\ WF_vars(ExpireAny)

MutualExclusion ==
  \A o \in ORs : Cardinality({t \in Teams : <<o, t>> \in grants}) <= 1

AllRequestsEventuallyGranted ==
  \A t \in Teams : (t \in requesting) ~> HasGrant(t)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Teams = {t1, t2, t3}
    ORs = {or1, or2}
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    LeaseLen = 2
    NoTeam = noteam
    NoInst = noinst
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY AllRequestsEventuallyGranted
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital runs two independent operating-room scheduling instances -- for example, one coordination process per wing -- but both instances draw from the very same shared pool of physical operating rooms rather than each owning a private subset. Surgical teams request time in an operating room; either scheduler instance may service a given request by granting the team a time-bounded lease on a free room. A granted lease starts at age zero and ages by one tick every time the system advances time, up to a fixed maximum lease length; once a lease reaches that maximum age it is automatically force-expired and the room becomes free again, or the team holding it may instead voluntarily release the room early before its lease expires. Because both scheduler instances read and write the same shared grant record before handing out a room, neither instance can grant a room that the other instance (or itself) has already granted to someone else.

The full action set is: (1) a team with no current room and no outstanding request submits a request for a room; (2) either scheduler instance grants a free room's lease to a team that has an outstanding request, recording which instance made the grant and resetting the room's lease age to zero; (3) time advances for a currently-leased room, incrementing its lease age by one, up to the maximum lease length; (4) a currently-leased room whose lease age has reached the maximum length is force-expired, clearing its grant and resetting its age; (5) a currently-leased room is voluntarily released early by its holding team before its lease has expired, clearing its grant and resetting its age.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for every operating room, at most one surgical team is recorded as currently holding an active lease on that room -- the shared pool is never mutually double-booked between the two independent scheduler instances.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every surgical team that submits a request for an operating room eventually receives a granted lease on some room, even though the pool is shared between two independent scheduler instances and rooms must first be freed up by expiry or voluntary release.

---- MODULE W4Od0m6p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Teams, Capacity, MaxLeaseTerm, MaxTime, MaxSeq

\* Lease-based ownership with expiry: a team's grant on shared OR capacity
\* auto-reclaims once its recorded expiry passes, even without a release
\* message. Because the network can reorder acquire/release messages, the
\* scheduler only applies a message whose sequence number is strictly newer
\* than the last one it already applied for that team -- this is what keeps
\* stale or duplicate deliveries from corrupting the capacity count below.

VARIABLES now, teamSeq, lastSeq, network, leaseHeld, leaseExpiry

vars == <<now, teamSeq, lastSeq, network, leaseHeld, leaseExpiry>>

Messages == Teams \X {"acquire", "release"} \X (1..MaxSeq)

TypeOK ==
    /\ now \in 0..MaxTime
    /\ teamSeq \in [Teams -> 0..MaxSeq]
    /\ lastSeq \in [Teams -> 0..MaxSeq]
    /\ network \subseteq Messages
    /\ leaseHeld \in [Teams -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ leaseExpiry \in [Teams -> 0..(MaxTime + MaxLeaseTerm)]

Init ==
    /\ now = 0
    /\ teamSeq = [t \in Teams |-> 0]
    /\ lastSeq = [t \in Teams |-> 0]
    /\ network = {}
    /\ leaseHeld = [t \in Teams |-> FALSE]
    /\ leaseExpiry = [t \in Teams |-> 0]

ActiveCount == Cardinality({t \in Teams : leaseHeld[t]})

SendAcquire(t) ==
    /\ ~leaseHeld[t]
    /\ teamSeq[t] < MaxSeq
    /\ teamSeq' = [teamSeq EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
    /\ network' = network \cup {<<t, "acquire", teamSeq[t] + 1>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, lastSeq, leaseHeld, leaseExpiry>>

SendRelease(t) ==
    /\ leaseHeld[t]
    /\ teamSeq[t] < MaxSeq
    /\ teamSeq' = [teamSeq EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
    /\ network' = network \cup {<<t, "release", teamSeq[t] + 1>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, lastSeq, leaseHeld, leaseExpiry>>

\* Delivery order is unconstrained (m ranges over the whole in-flight set),
\* which is exactly what lets the network reorder messages.
DeliverMessage(m) ==
    /\ m \in network
    /\ network' = network \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, teamSeq>>
    /\ IF m[3] <= lastSeq[m[1]]
       THEN UNCHANGED <<lastSeq, leaseHeld, leaseExpiry>>
       ELSE
         /\ lastSeq' = [lastSeq EXCEPT ![m[1]] = m[3]]
         /\ IF m[2] = "acquire"
            THEN IF ActiveCount < Capacity
                 THEN /\ leaseHeld' = [leaseHeld EXCEPT ![m[1]] = TRUE]
                      /\ leaseExpiry' = [leaseExpiry EXCEPT ![m[1]] = now + MaxLeaseTerm]
                 ELSE UNCHANGED <<leaseHeld, leaseExpiry>>
            ELSE
                 /\ leaseHeld' = [leaseHeld EXCEPT ![m[1]] = FALSE]
                 /\ UNCHANGED leaseExpiry

ExpireLease(t) ==
    /\ leaseHeld[t]
    /\ now >= leaseExpiry[t]
    /\ leaseHeld' = [leaseHeld EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, teamSeq, lastSeq, network, leaseExpiry>>

Tick ==
    /\ now < MaxTime
    /\ now' = now + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<teamSeq, lastSeq, network, leaseHeld, leaseExpiry>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams : SendAcquire(t) \/ SendRelease(t) \/ ExpireLease(t)
    \/ \E m \in network : DeliverMessage(m)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded, regardless of message reordering.
BoundedCapacity == ActiveCount <= Capacity

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Teams = {T1, T2, T3}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxLeaseTerm = 1
    MaxTime = 2
    MaxSeq = 2
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital's operating-room scheduler controls how many procedures may run at once, bounded by the number of anesthesia teams the hospital can staff at the same time (its concurrency capacity), not by the number of physical rooms. Surgical teams request a time-bounded lease on that shared capacity before starting a procedure, and must eventually release it (or let it expire) when done. Communication between a surgical team's terminal and the central scheduler runs over an unreliable hospital network where acquire and release messages can be reordered in transit -- a release sent after an acquire can arrive at the scheduler before it, or a stale duplicate can arrive late -- so the scheduler tags every message with a per-team sequence number and only honors a message if its sequence number is strictly newer than the last one it already applied for that team; older or duplicate messages are silently dropped.

The full set of actions is:
1. SendAcquire(t): a team t that does not currently hold a capacity lease sends a freshly sequenced "acquire" message into the network.
2. SendRelease(t): a team t that currently holds a capacity lease sends a freshly sequenced "release" message into the network.
3. DeliverMessage(m): the scheduler picks any message currently in the network (delivery order is unconstrained, modeling reordering) and processes it: if the message's sequence number is not newer than the last one already applied for that team, it is dropped with no effect; otherwise the scheduler records it as the newest applied sequence number for that team, and if it is an "acquire" it grants the lease (recording an expiry time) only if the number of currently held leases is still below capacity, and if it is a "release" it frees the team's lease immediately.
4. ExpireLease(t): a team t holding a lease whose recorded expiry time has passed has its lease reclaimed automatically by the scheduler, even if no release message was ever delivered.
5. Tick: the global clock advances by one unit, up to a bounded horizon.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of teams simultaneously holding a granted capacity lease never exceeds the hospital's fixed concurrency capacity, no matter what order the acquire, release, and expiry events are delivered or interleaved in.

---- MODULE W4Od0m8p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Teams, NumWings, RoomsPerWing, NoneT, NoneR

\* Hierarchical locking: a team must hold a wing's coarse lock before it can
\* take a room's fine lock, and only then may it actually operate. The
\* invariant protects mutual exclusion of the critical resource (the room)
\* itself. Teams may be arbitrarily slow between phases (the twist) but never
\* fail, which is what the per-team fairness conditions in Spec encode.

Wings == 1..NumWings
Rooms == 1..(NumWings * RoomsPerWing)
WingOf(r) == ((r - 1) \div RoomsPerWing) + 1

VARIABLES wingLock, roomLock, teamPhase, teamRoom

vars == <<wingLock, roomLock, teamPhase, teamRoom>>

Phases == {"idle", "hasWing", "hasRoom", "operating", "done"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ wingLock \in [Wings -> Teams \cup {NoneT}]
    /\ roomLock \in [Rooms -> Teams \cup {NoneT}]
    /\ teamPhase \in [Teams -> Phases]
    /\ teamRoom \in [Teams -> Rooms \cup {NoneR}]

Init ==
    /\ wingLock = [w \in Wings |-> NoneT]
    /\ roomLock = [r \in Rooms |-> NoneT]
    /\ teamPhase = [t \in Teams |-> "idle"]
    /\ teamRoom = [t \in Teams |-> NoneR]

AcquireWing(t) ==
    /\ teamPhase[t] = "idle"
    /\ \E r \in Rooms :
        /\ wingLock[WingOf(r)] = NoneT
        /\ wingLock' = [wingLock EXCEPT ![WingOf(r)] = t]
        /\ teamRoom' = [teamRoom EXCEPT ![t] = r]
    /\ teamPhase' = [teamPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "hasWing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED roomLock

AcquireRoom(t) ==
    /\ teamPhase[t] = "hasWing"
    /\ roomLock[teamRoom[t]] = NoneT
    /\ roomLock' = [roomLock EXCEPT ![teamRoom[t]] = t]
    /\ teamPhase' = [teamPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "hasRoom"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wingLock, teamRoom>>

StartOperation(t) ==
    /\ teamPhase[t] = "hasRoom"
    /\ teamPhase' = [teamPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "operating"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wingLock, roomLock, teamRoom>>

FinishOperation(t) ==
    /\ teamPhase[t] = "operating"
    /\ roomLock' = [roomLock EXCEPT ![teamRoom[t]] = NoneT]
    /\ teamPhase' = [teamPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wingLock, teamRoom>>

ReleaseWing(t) ==
    /\ teamPhase[t] = "done"
    /\ wingLock' = [wingLock EXCEPT ![WingOf(teamRoom[t])] = NoneT]
    /\ teamRoom' = [teamRoom EXCEPT ![t] = NoneR]
    /\ teamPhase' = [teamPhase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED roomLock

Next == \E t \in Teams :
    AcquireWing(t) \/ AcquireRoom(t) \/ StartOperation(t) \/ FinishOperation(t) \/ ReleaseWing(t)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A t \in Teams :
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireWing(t))
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireRoom(t))
        /\ WF_vars(StartOperation(t))
        /\ WF_vars(FinishOperation(t))
        /\ WF_vars(ReleaseWing(t))

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: no room ever has two teams
\* simultaneously operating in it.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A r \in Rooms : Cardinality({t \in Teams : teamPhase[t] = "operating" /\ teamRoom[t] = r}) <= 1

TeamEventuallyIdle == \A t \in Teams : (teamPhase[t] # "idle") ~> (teamPhase[t] = "idle")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Teams = {T1, T2, T3}
    NumWings = 2
    RoomsPerWing = 2
    NoneT = NoneT
    NoneR = NoneR
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY TeamEventuallyIdle
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital's operating-room scheduler organizes rooms into wings; each wing has several operating rooms nested inside it. A surgical team that wants to use a specific operating room must first take that wing's coarse-grained lock, and only then take the fine-grained lock on the specific room itself, before it may actually begin operating -- the operating room is the critical resource, and only one surgical team may be actively operating in it at a time. A team can be slow at any phase -- it may take an arbitrarily long time between taking the room's lock and actually starting the operation, or between finishing the operation and releasing its locks -- but it never fails or abandons a lock it holds, so it always eventually finishes its full cycle and frees the room for the next team.

The full set of actions is:
1. AcquireWing(t): an idle team picks some operating room and, if that room's wing lock is free, takes the wing lock and records which room it intends to use.
2. AcquireRoom(t): a team holding its chosen room's wing lock takes the room's own fine-grained lock, if it is free.
3. StartOperation(t): a team holding both locks on its room (and which may have been slow up to this point) begins actively operating in that room.
4. FinishOperation(t): a team actively operating in its room finishes and releases the room's fine-grained lock, without yet releasing the wing lock.
5. ReleaseWing(t): a team that has finished its operation releases the wing lock and returns to idle, free to request a different room later.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for every operating room, at most one surgical team is actively operating in it at the same time -- the hierarchical coarse-then-fine locking guarantees mutual exclusion of that critical resource.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every surgical team that leaves the idle state to begin a new case eventually returns to idle, having completed its operation and released both locks, even though it may be arbitrarily slow along the way, because it never fails.

---- MODULE W4Od1m9p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Vals, MaxEpoch, InitVal, NoVal

\* An air-traffic runway allocator keeps one shared configuration record (the
\* active runway assignment payload). Ground controllers submit updates to
\* it tagged with the reconfiguration epoch in force when they were sent.
\* The network can deliver in-flight update messages in any order, so a
\* message stamped with an old epoch can arrive after a newer one has
\* already been applied. Epoch-numbered fencing rejects any message whose
\* epoch is behind the record's current epoch, which is what stops a
\* reordered stale message from clobbering (losing) a newer update.
\* The invariant ties the live record back to a ghost log of every accepted
\* update, so it fails if fencing ever lets a stale write silently win.

VARIABLES currentEpoch, recordEpoch, record, inflight, log

TypeOK ==
  /\ currentEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ recordEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ record \in Vals \cup {NoVal}
  /\ inflight \subseteq [epoch : 0..MaxEpoch, val : Vals, by : Controllers]
  /\ log \subseteq (0..MaxEpoch) \times Vals

Init ==
  /\ currentEpoch = 0
  /\ recordEpoch = 0
  /\ record = InitVal
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ log = {}

Reconfigure ==
  /\ currentEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ currentEpoch' = currentEpoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<recordEpoch, record, inflight, log>>

SubmitUpdate(c, v) ==
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[epoch |-> currentEpoch, val |-> v, by |-> c]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<currentEpoch, recordEpoch, record, log>>

DeliverAccept(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ m.epoch >= recordEpoch
  /\ record' = m.val
  /\ recordEpoch' = m.epoch
  /\ log' = log \cup {<<m.epoch, m.val>>}
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED currentEpoch

DeliverReject(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ m.epoch < recordEpoch
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<currentEpoch, recordEpoch, record, log>>

ExpireStale(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ m.epoch < currentEpoch
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<currentEpoch, recordEpoch, record, log>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, v \in Vals : SubmitUpdate(c, v)
  \/ \E m \in inflight : DeliverAccept(m)
  \/ \E m \in inflight : DeliverReject(m)
  \/ \E m \in inflight : ExpireStale(m)

vars == <<currentEpoch, recordEpoch, record, inflight, log>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdates ==
  /\ \A p \in log : p[1] <= recordEpoch
  /\ (log # {} => \E v \in Vals : <<recordEpoch, v>> \in log /\ record = v)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    Vals = {v1, v2}
    MaxEpoch = 1
    InitVal = v1
    NoVal = noval
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An air-traffic control facility keeps one shared runway-configuration record that several ground controllers can update -- for example, which runways are currently active for departures. The facility uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration: whenever the controller roster changes (a handoff, a shift change, or a failover), the system's reconfiguration epoch is bumped. Every update a controller sends to the shared record is stamped with whatever epoch was current at the moment it was sent, and then queued as an in-flight message. Because the underlying messaging network can reorder, delay, or duplicate delivery timing, in-flight update messages are not necessarily delivered in the order they were sent -- a message stamped with an old epoch can still be sitting in flight and arrive after a message from a newer epoch has already been applied to the record.

To keep an old, reordered message from silently clobbering a newer one, every delivered message is fenced by its epoch: a message is only allowed to actually update the shared record if its stamped epoch is at least as new as the epoch already recorded there; otherwise the message is simply discarded as stale. In-flight messages whose epoch has fallen behind the facility's current reconfiguration epoch can also be proactively expired/garbage-collected from the network before they are ever delivered.

The full set of actions is: (1) reconfigure -- bump the facility's current epoch by one (representing a controller-roster change); (2) a controller submits an update carrying a value and the epoch that was current when it was sent, adding it to the set of in-flight messages; (3) deliver-and-accept an in-flight message whose stamped epoch is at least as new as the record's current epoch, applying its value to the shared record, advancing the record's epoch to match, and appending the accepted (epoch, value) pair to a permanent log of every update that was ever actually applied; (4) deliver-and-reject an in-flight message whose stamped epoch is older than the record's current epoch, discarding it without changing the record; (5) expire an in-flight message whose stamped epoch has fallen behind the facility's current reconfiguration epoch, removing it from the network before it is ever delivered.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the record's current epoch is never older than the epoch of any update that was ever actually accepted and logged, and whenever anything has been accepted, the record's live value still matches exactly the value that was logged for the record's current epoch -- so a reordered, stale-epoch message can never silently overwrite (lose) a newer update.

---- MODULE W4Od11m9p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Processes, NoneP, MaxEpoch

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration grants exclusive use of one press to one
\* controller at a time. Grant/Release messages travel over a network
\* modeled as a SET (delivery order is nondeterministic, i.e. reorderable).
\* The invariant protects mutual exclusion: fencing on the message's epoch
\* against the coordinator's live epoch must stop a stale, reordered Grant
\* from ever letting a second controller start using the press.
VARIABLES epoch, assigned, network, holding, procEpoch

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ assigned = NoneP
    /\ network = {}
    /\ holding = {}
    /\ procEpoch = [p \in Processes |-> 0]

Reconfigure ==
    \* Bumping the epoch is a hard fence: the press's own control firmware
    \* only accepts commands stamped with the live epoch, so any process
    \* still believing it holds the press is immediately fenced off here,
    \* even if it has not yet heard about the reconfiguration itself.
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ assigned' = NoneP
    /\ holding' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<network, procEpoch>>

GrantAccess ==
    /\ assigned = NoneP
    /\ \E p \in Processes :
         /\ assigned' = p
         /\ network' = network \cup {[type |-> "Grant", ep |-> epoch, proc |-> p]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holding, procEpoch>>

DeliverGrant ==
    \E m \in network :
        /\ m.type = "Grant"
        /\ network' = network \ {m}
        /\ procEpoch' = [procEpoch EXCEPT ![m.proc] =
                            IF m.ep > procEpoch[m.proc] THEN m.ep ELSE procEpoch[m.proc]]
        /\ holding' = IF m.ep = epoch THEN holding \cup {m.proc} ELSE holding
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assigned>>

ReleaseHolding ==
    \E p \in Processes :
        /\ p \in holding
        /\ holding' = holding \ {p}
        /\ network' = network \cup {[type |-> "Release", ep |-> procEpoch[p], proc |-> p]}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, assigned, procEpoch>>

DeliverRelease ==
    \E m \in network :
        /\ m.type = "Release"
        /\ network' = network \ {m}
        /\ assigned' = IF (m.ep = epoch /\ assigned = m.proc) THEN NoneP ELSE assigned
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holding, procEpoch>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ GrantAccess
    \/ DeliverGrant
    \/ ReleaseHolding
    \/ DeliverRelease

vars == <<epoch, assigned, network, holding, procEpoch>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: mutual exclusion of the press -- never more than one live holder.
PressMutualExclusion == Cardinality(holding) <= 1

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Processes = {q1, q2, q3}
    NoneP = none
    MaxEpoch = 3
INVARIANT PressMutualExclusion
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A print shop runs a single expensive color press as its one critical resource, shared by several print-controller processes. A coordinator hands out access using epoch-numbered reconfiguration: whenever the coordinator needs to change who may use the press (for example after detecting a controller has gone quiet), it bumps a monotonically increasing epoch number and revokes the previous designee before naming a new one for the new epoch. Grants and releases travel as separate messages over an asynchronous network, and the twist is that this network can reorder messages arbitrarily -- a Grant message sent in an old epoch can sit in flight and be delivered only after the coordinator has already reconfigured and granted the press to someone else in a later epoch. Controllers therefore only stamp the press as "in use" locally if the epoch carried by a delivered Grant message still equals the coordinator's live epoch at delivery time; grants tagged with a stale, already-superseded epoch are absorbed into a controller's bookkeeping (it records having seen that epoch) but never actually let the controller start using the press.

The full set of actions is:
1. Reconfigure: the coordinator bumps the epoch (bounded by a maximum epoch count) and clears the current designee. The press's own firmware only accepts commands stamped with the live epoch, so bumping the epoch is itself a hard fence that immediately revokes whoever was previously using the press in the old epoch, even before that controller has heard about the reconfiguration.
2. GrantAccess: when no controller is currently designated in the live epoch, the coordinator designates one controller and places a Grant message (carrying that epoch and the controller's identity) into the in-flight network.
3. DeliverGrant: any Grant message currently sitting in the network (regardless of send order) may be delivered to its addressed controller; the controller updates its locally-known epoch to the message's epoch if it is newer, and only adds itself to the set of controllers actually using the press if the message's epoch still equals the coordinator's current live epoch.
4. ReleaseHolding: a controller that is using the press stops using it and places a Release message (carrying its epoch and identity) into the in-flight network.
5. DeliverRelease: any Release message currently sitting in the network may be delivered to the coordinator; if the message's epoch matches the coordinator's live epoch and the message's controller is still the live designee, the coordinator clears the designee so a new grant can be issued.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one controller is ever recorded as actually using the press at the same time, even though Grant and Release messages may be delivered out of the order they were sent.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m7p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Drones, NoneD, MaxTerm

\* Controller authority is handed out via a compare-and-swap register (the
\* term counter). Drones sync their own view of the term lazily, so a drone
\* can hold a stale belief that it is still the controller after another
\* drone has since won a later election. One drone may crash silently. The
\* invariant protects against any crashed/unauthorized/stale drone ever
\* getting a command logged as authorized.
VARIABLES term, leader, crashed, refreshedTerm, leaderAtTerm, actionsLog

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoneD
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ refreshedTerm = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ leaderAtTerm = [t \in 0..MaxTerm |-> NoneD]
    /\ actionsLog = {}

\* The term counter wraps within a bounded range (a realistic detail of a
\* real CAS version register) instead of hitting a hard ceiling, so a live
\* drone can always eventually win a fresh election no matter how many
\* elections have already happened -- this is what keeps the swarm from
\* getting permanently stuck if the current controller silently crashes.
\* When a term slot is reused, stale log entries tagged with that slot are
\* evicted (they described a strictly earlier cycle's controller for that
\* slot, which is no longer the one recorded in leaderAtTerm).
Elect(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ refreshedTerm[d] = term
    /\ LET nt == IF term = MaxTerm THEN 0 ELSE term + 1 IN
         /\ term' = nt
         /\ leader' = d
         /\ leaderAtTerm' = [leaderAtTerm EXCEPT ![nt] = d]
         /\ refreshedTerm' = [refreshedTerm EXCEPT ![d] = nt]
         /\ actionsLog' = {e \in actionsLog : e[2] # nt}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed>>

Refresh(d) ==
    \* Since the term counter wraps, a drone's synced value can end up
    \* numerically "ahead" of the live term after a wrap; the poll simply
    \* re-syncs to whatever the live term currently reads, in either
    \* direction, rather than only catching up an ordered lag.
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ refreshedTerm[d] # term
    /\ refreshedTerm' = [refreshedTerm EXCEPT ![d] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, crashed, leaderAtTerm, actionsLog>>

IssueControlAction(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ refreshedTerm[d] = term
    /\ leader = d
    /\ actionsLog' = actionsLog \cup {<<d, term>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, crashed, refreshedTerm, leaderAtTerm>>

CrashSilently(d) ==
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, refreshedTerm, leaderAtTerm, actionsLog>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Elect(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Refresh(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : IssueControlAction(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : CrashSilently(d)

vars == <<term, leader, crashed, refreshedTerm, leaderAtTerm, actionsLog>>

Fairness ==
    \A d \in Drones :
        /\ SF_vars(Elect(d))
        /\ WF_vars(Refresh(d))
        /\ SF_vars(IssueControlAction(d))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: every logged command's drone matches the true recorded controller for its term.
NoStaleOrUnauthorizedAction ==
    \A e \in actionsLog : leaderAtTerm[e[2]] = e[1]

EventuallyAuthorizedAction == <>(actionsLog # {})

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
    NoneD = none
    MaxTerm = 2
INVARIANT NoStaleOrUnauthorizedAction
PROPERTY EventuallyAuthorizedAction
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm of drones takes turns being the mission controller authorized to issue zone re-tasking commands to the rest of the fleet. Authority is handed out through a single shared compare-and-swap register holding a term number: a drone that wants to become controller reads its own last-synced copy of the term and attempts to CAS the shared register forward -- the attempt only succeeds if its synced copy still equals the register's live term, atomically bumping the term and recording that drone as the live controller. Drones do not learn about a new election the instant it happens; each drone must separately refresh its own synced copy of the term (and of who currently holds it) by polling the register, so a drone's local view of "am I the controller" can lag behind reality. The twist is that exactly one drone in the swarm can crash silently at any point -- it simply stops doing anything further, with no notification broadcast to the rest of the swarm.

The full set of actions is:
1. Elect: a non-crashed drone whose last-synced term still equals the register's live term attempts the compare-and-swap; on success the term counter advances to its next value within a bounded range (wrapping back around instead of ever hitting a hard ceiling, so a live drone can always eventually win a fresh election even after many elections have already happened), that drone becomes the recorded live controller, the register's per-term-slot controller history is updated to record who now holds that slot, the drone's own synced term is updated to match immediately, and any previously logged command that was tagged with the now-reused term slot is retired from the log (it described a strictly earlier cycle's controller for that slot).
2. Refresh: a non-crashed drone whose synced term does not currently match the register's live term polls the register and brings its synced term up to date; because the term counter wraps, a drone's synced value can end up numerically ahead of the live term right after a wrap, so this simply re-syncs to whatever the register currently reads rather than only catching up a lag.
3. IssueControlAction: a non-crashed drone may issue a zone re-tasking command, which is logged as an authorized action, but only if its currently synced term equals the register's live term AND it is in fact the drone recorded as the live controller -- a drone acting on a synced term that has fallen behind (i.e. it missed a later election) is not authorized and cannot log a command.
4. CrashSilently: exactly one, as-yet-unaffected drone in the swarm may crash; once crashed it can never again attempt an election, refresh, or issue a command, and no message informs the rest of the swarm that this happened.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, every zone re-tasking command ever logged as authorized was in fact issued by the drone that the register's per-term history records as the true live controller for the term recorded alongside that command -- no crashed, unauthorized, or stale-term drone's command is ever logged as authorized.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Despite the possibility that any one drone silently crashes at any point, the swarm eventually logs at least one authorized zone re-tasking command, i.e. the surviving drones eventually complete a legitimate election and successfully issue a command.

---- MODULE W4Od14m9p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxEpoch

\* A wildfire surveillance drone swarm is coordinated by an epoch-numbered
\* roster: ground control periodically reconfigures which drones are
\* currently authorized to file detection reports, bumping a global epoch
\* number each time. A drone learns of a reconfiguration only when it
\* catches up to the current epoch -- it may be slow to do so (patchy field
\* connectivity), but it never simply fails; it always eventually catches up.
\* The invariant protects the fact that only a drone that is both caught up
\* to the current epoch AND a member of the current roster ever gets a
\* report accepted -- a stale or unauthorized drone's attempt is dropped.

VARIABLES epoch, roster, droneEpoch, reports

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ roster \subseteq Drones
    /\ droneEpoch \in [Drones -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ reports \subseteq Drones

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ roster = Drones
    /\ droneEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ reports = {}

\* Ground control reconfigures the swarm: the epoch advances and a new
\* (nonempty) authorized roster takes effect. The report window resets, since
\* reports are scoped to the epoch during which they were filed.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \E newRoster \in (SUBSET Drones) \ {{}} :
        /\ roster' = newRoster
        /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ reports' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED droneEpoch

\* The slow-but-not-failed twist: a drone that is behind eventually receives
\* and processes the latest reconfiguration, catching its own epoch up to
\* the current one, however long that takes.
CatchUp(d) ==
    /\ droneEpoch[d] < epoch
    /\ droneEpoch' = [droneEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, reports>>

\* A drone that is both caught up and on the current roster may file a
\* report for this epoch.
SubmitReport(d) ==
    /\ droneEpoch[d] = epoch
    /\ d \in roster
    /\ d \notin reports
    /\ reports' = reports \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, droneEpoch>>

\* A stale (behind on epoch) or unauthorized (not on the current roster)
\* drone attempts to file a report; ground control drops the attempt, so it
\* has no effect on the accepted report set.
AttemptStaleSubmit(d) ==
    /\ (droneEpoch[d] # epoch \/ d \notin roster)
    /\ d \notin reports
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, droneEpoch, reports>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E d \in Drones : CatchUp(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : SubmitReport(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : AttemptStaleSubmit(d)

vars == <<epoch, roster, droneEpoch, reports>>

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A d \in Drones : WF_vars(CatchUp(d))

\* Every drone allowed to act right now is both caught up to the current
\* epoch and on the current roster; the report set never holds an entry
\* filed by a stale or unauthorized drone.
AuthorizedNow == {d \in Drones : droneEpoch[d] = epoch /\ d \in roster}

NoStaleOrUnauthorizedAction == reports \subseteq AuthorizedNow

\* Whenever the swarm is past its initial epoch, every drone eventually
\* catches up to the current epoch -- reconfiguration always completes,
\* even though catching up can take an arbitrarily slow drone arbitrarily
\* long, as long as it never permanently fails.
AllCaughtUp == \A d \in Drones : droneEpoch[d] = epoch

ReconfigurationEventuallyCompletes == (epoch > 0) ~> AllCaughtUp

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT NoStaleOrUnauthorizedAction
PROPERTY ReconfigurationEventuallyCompletes
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A swarm of drones surveys a wildfire perimeter, coordinated by ground control through an epoch-numbered roster. At any time there is a current epoch number and a current roster of drones authorized to file detection reports during that epoch. When conditions change (a drone's battery runs low, a new drone launches, the fire front shifts), ground control reconfigures the swarm: it advances the epoch and installs a new authorized roster. A drone learns of a reconfiguration only by catching up to the current epoch, which can take an arbitrarily long time if its field connectivity is patchy -- it may be slow, but it never simply fails; it always eventually catches up. Because catching up can lag, a drone may sometimes still believe it is operating under an old epoch or may no longer be on the current roster, and any report it tries to file under those conditions must not be accepted.

The full set of actions is:
1. Reconfigure: ground control advances the epoch and installs a new, nonempty authorized roster; the report set for the new epoch starts empty.
2. CatchUp: a drone that is behind the current epoch (patchy connectivity, but not failed) receives and processes the latest reconfiguration, bringing its own known epoch up to the current one.
3. SubmitReport: a drone that is both caught up to the current epoch and a member of the current roster files a detection report, which is accepted into the report set for this epoch.
4. AttemptStaleSubmit: a drone that is either behind on the epoch or no longer on the current roster tries to file a report anyway; ground control drops the attempt, leaving the accepted report set unchanged.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, every drone whose report has been accepted for the current epoch is both caught up to that epoch and a member of the current roster -- no stale or unauthorized drone's report is ever accepted.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the swarm has been reconfigured at least once, every drone eventually catches up to the current epoch, so reconfiguration always completes and no drone is left permanently stale, even though an individual drone may take an arbitrarily long (but not infinite) time to catch up.

---- MODULE W4Od15m5p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Orders, Nodes, MaxCapacity, Quorum

\* Opening-auction admission requires a quorum of replica-node votes per
\* order. Votes travel as messages in a SET (delivery is nondeterministic,
\* i.e. reorderable) rather than a sequence. The invariant protects the
\* book's fixed capacity, re-checked at the moment of admission itself so
\* reordered votes can never let quorum-reaching proposals overrun it.
VARIABLES book, proposed, voteMsgs, tally

Init ==
    /\ book = {}
    /\ proposed = {}
    /\ voteMsgs = {}
    /\ tally = [o \in Orders |-> {}]

Propose(o) ==
    /\ o \notin book
    /\ o \notin proposed
    /\ proposed' = proposed \cup {o}
    /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![o] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, voteMsgs>>

CastVote(o, n) ==
    /\ o \in proposed
    /\ n \notin tally[o]
    /\ voteMsgs' = voteMsgs \cup {[order |-> o, voter |-> n]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, proposed, tally>>

DeliverVote ==
    \E m \in voteMsgs :
        /\ voteMsgs' = voteMsgs \ {m}
        /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![m.order] = @ \cup {m.voter}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, proposed>>

CommitOrder(o) ==
    /\ o \in proposed
    /\ Cardinality(tally[o]) >= Quorum
    /\ Cardinality(book) < MaxCapacity
    /\ book' = book \cup {o}
    /\ proposed' = proposed \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voteMsgs, tally>>

WithdrawProposal(o) ==
    /\ o \in proposed
    /\ Cardinality(tally[o]) < Quorum
    /\ proposed' = proposed \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, voteMsgs, tally>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Propose(o)
    \/ \E o \in Orders, n \in Nodes : CastVote(o, n)
    \/ DeliverVote
    \/ \E o \in Orders : CommitOrder(o)
    \/ \E o \in Orders : WithdrawProposal(o)

vars == <<book, proposed, voteMsgs, tally>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: the auction book's fixed capacity is never exceeded.
BoundedAuctionCapacity == Cardinality(book) <= MaxCapacity

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Orders = {o1, o2, o3}
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    MaxCapacity = 2
    Quorum = 2
INVARIANT BoundedAuctionCapacity
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction across several matching-engine replica nodes. Before any order can be admitted into the fixed-capacity opening-auction book, it must be proposed and then win a quorum of votes from the replica nodes -- no single node can unilaterally admit an order. Votes travel to a shared tally as individual vote messages over an asynchronous network, and the twist is that this network can reorder those vote messages arbitrarily: a vote cast early for one proposal round can be delivered late, and votes for different orders can be delivered in any interleaving relative to each other and relative to new proposals being raised. Regardless of how votes arrive, an order is only ever actually admitted into the book once its tally reaches quorum AND the book still has room -- the book's fixed capacity is checked again at the moment of admission, not just when votes are being collected, so no burst of quorum-reaching proposals can ever push the book past its bound.

The full set of actions is:
1. Propose: an order that is not already in the book and not already under proposal is put forward for a fresh voting round, with its vote tally reset to empty for this round.
2. CastVote: a replica node that has not yet had its vote counted for a proposed order sends a vote message for that order out onto the network.
3. DeliverVote: any vote message currently in flight on the network -- regardless of when it was sent relative to other in-flight messages -- may be delivered, adding its voting node to that order's tally.
4. CommitOrder: a proposed order whose tally has reached quorum is admitted into the book, but only if the book has not already reached its fixed capacity; the proposal is then cleared.
5. WithdrawProposal: a proposed order whose tally has not yet reached quorum may be withdrawn from consideration, freeing it to be proposed again later in a fresh round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of orders admitted into the opening-auction book never exceeds the book's fixed capacity, no matter how many vote messages are reordered or how many proposals simultaneously reach quorum.

---- MODULE W4Od15m7p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Orders, Slots, NoOwner, NoSlot

\* Models a stock exchange opening-auction slot allocator: each matching-engine
\* slot is guarded by a compare-and-swap register (owner + version). Claim
\* messages travel over a network that can reorder and duplicate them, so a
\* stale claim must be rejected by the version check rather than accepted.
\* The invariant protects against a slot ever being double-allocated to two
\* different orders, or an order's local record disagreeing with the slot's
\* authoritative CAS register.

VARIABLES slotOwner, slotVersion, orderSlot, msgs, phase

TypeOK ==
    /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Orders \cup {NoOwner}]
    /\ slotVersion \in [Slots -> Nat]
    /\ orderSlot \in [Orders -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ msgs \subseteq [order: Orders, slot: Slots, version: Nat]
    /\ phase \in {"open", "closed"}

Init ==
    /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> NoOwner]
    /\ slotVersion = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ orderSlot = [o \in Orders |-> NoSlot]
    /\ msgs = {}
    /\ phase = "open"

\* An order broadcasts a claim for a slot, stamped with the version it last
\* observed. Because msgs is a set, repeated sends of an identical claim are
\* idempotent, and the network is free to deliver any pending claim next,
\* modeling reordering.
SendClaim(o, s) ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ orderSlot[o] = NoSlot
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[order |-> o, slot |-> s, version |-> slotVersion[s]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, orderSlot, phase>>

\* The CAS succeeds only if the message's version still matches the slot's
\* current version AND the slot is unclaimed AND the order has not already
\* been satisfied by some other (possibly reordered) claim.
DeliverSuccess(m) ==
    /\ m \in msgs
    /\ slotOwner[m.slot] = NoOwner
    /\ slotVersion[m.slot] = m.version
    /\ orderSlot[m.order] = NoSlot
    /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![m.slot] = m.order]
    /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![m.slot] = @ + 1]
    /\ orderSlot' = [orderSlot EXCEPT ![m.order] = m.slot]
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED phase

\* The CAS is rejected -- either the slot was already taken, the order was
\* already satisfied elsewhere, or (the reordering hazard) the version has
\* moved on since this claim was issued -- and the stale message is dropped.
DeliverFail(m) ==
    /\ m \in msgs
    /\ ~(slotOwner[m.slot] = NoOwner /\ slotVersion[m.slot] = m.version /\ orderSlot[m.order] = NoSlot)
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, orderSlot, phase>>

\* The exchange cuts the auction over to continuous matching at some
\* nondeterministic point; already in-flight claims still drain afterward,
\* but no new claims may be sent once trading has moved on.
CloseAuction ==
    /\ phase = "open"
    /\ phase' = "closed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, orderSlot, msgs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in Slots : SendClaim(o, s)
    \/ \E m \in msgs : DeliverSuccess(m)
    \/ \E m \in msgs : DeliverFail(m)
    \/ CloseAuction

vars == <<slotOwner, slotVersion, orderSlot, msgs, phase>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The set of orders that believe they hold slot s can never be more than the
\* single order the slot's CAS register actually attributes it to -- so a
\* slot is never handed out twice, even to reordered/duplicated claims.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        {o \in Orders : orderSlot[o] = s} \subseteq
            (IF slotOwner[s] = NoOwner THEN {} ELSE {slotOwner[s]})

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Orders = {o1, o2, o3}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    NoOwner = NoOwner
    NoSlot = NoSlot
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
At a stock exchange's opening auction, incoming orders must each be assigned to exactly one of a small number of matching-engine slots before continuous trading begins. Each slot is guarded by a compare-and-swap register that pairs a current owner (or "none") with a version number. To claim a slot, an order sends a claim message over the network stamped with the version it last observed for that slot; the network is unreliable in the sense that claim messages can be reordered and duplicated, so a stale claim issued before some other order already grabbed the slot might arrive and be processed only after the slot's version has already moved on.

The full set of actions is:
1. SendClaim: an order that does not yet hold a slot broadcasts a claim for some slot, stamped with the slot's version as the order currently observes it. This can happen only while the auction is still open, and duplicate broadcasts of an identical claim have no additional effect.
2. DeliverSuccess: the network delivers a pending claim message and the compare-and-swap succeeds -- the slot is currently unclaimed, the message's stamped version still matches the slot's current version, and the order has not already been satisfied by some other claim -- so the slot's registered owner and version are updated and the order's own record is set to that slot.
3. DeliverFail: the network delivers a pending claim message but the compare-and-swap is rejected, because the slot was already taken, the order was already satisfied elsewhere, or (the reordering hazard) the slot's version has moved on since the claim was stamped; the stale message is simply dropped with no effect on any register.
4. CloseAuction: at some point the exchange cuts the auction over to continuous trading; from then on no new claims may be sent, though any claims still in flight continue to be delivered (and accepted or rejected) as usual.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for every slot, the set of orders whose own record says they hold that slot is never more than the single order the slot's compare-and-swap register actually attributes it to -- so, even with reordered or duplicated claim messages, no slot is ever handed out to two different orders.

---- MODULE W4Od15m8p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Slots, NoneI

\* Two independent opening-auction engines (Instances) share one pool of
\* allocation slots (Slots). Each engine must first grab the coarse lock on
\* the whole pool, then a fine-grained lock on one specific slot, before it
\* is allowed to grant itself that slot. The coarse lock keeps the two
\* engines from interleaving their per-slot bookkeeping on the same slot.

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, allocated, status

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarseLock \in Instances \cup {NoneI}
  /\ fineLock \in [Slots -> Instances \cup {NoneI}]
  /\ allocated \in [Slots -> SUBSET Instances]
  /\ status \in [Instances -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine", "done", "released"}]

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = NoneI
  /\ fineLock = [s \in Slots |-> NoneI]
  /\ allocated = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
  /\ status = [i \in Instances |-> "idle"]

AcquireCoarse(i) ==
  /\ status[i] = "idle"
  /\ coarseLock = NoneI
  /\ coarseLock' = i
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, allocated>>

AcquireFine(i, s) ==
  /\ status[i] = "coarse"
  /\ coarseLock = i
  /\ fineLock[s] = NoneI
  /\ allocated[s] = {}
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = i]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "fine"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, allocated>>

Allocate(i, s) ==
  /\ status[i] = "fine"
  /\ fineLock[s] = i
  /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![s] = allocated[s] \cup {i}]
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoneI]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

ReleaseCoarse(i) ==
  /\ status[i] = "done"
  /\ coarseLock = i
  /\ coarseLock' = NoneI
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "released"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, allocated>>

Next ==
  \/ (\E i \in Instances : AcquireCoarse(i))
  \/ (\E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : AcquireFine(i, s))
  \/ (\E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : Allocate(i, s))
  \/ (\E i \in Instances : ReleaseCoarse(i))

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, allocated, status>>

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A i \in Instances : WF_vars(AcquireCoarse(i))
  /\ \A i \in Instances : WF_vars(\E s \in Slots : AcquireFine(i, s))
  /\ \A i \in Instances : WF_vars(\E s \in Slots : Allocate(i, s))
  /\ \A i \in Instances : WF_vars(ReleaseCoarse(i))

\* Safety: a slot's grant set never grows past one engine -- the
\* coarse-then-fine discipline never lets two engines both believe they
\* hold the same slot in the shared pool.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slots : \A i, j \in Instances :
    (i \in allocated[s] /\ j \in allocated[s]) => i = j

EventuallyAllServed == <>(\A i \in Instances : status[i] = "released")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    Slots = {s1, s2, s3}
    NoneI = none
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY EventuallyAllServed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: Two independent opening-auction engines run the pre-market cross for two different listing venues, but both engines draw their per-symbol allocation slots from a single shared slot pool operated by the exchange's matching infrastructure. Before an engine may record itself as the owner of any slot in the shared pool, it must first acquire a coarse lock on the whole pool (so the two engines' bookkeeping steps never interleave arbitrarily), and only then acquire a fine-grained lock on the one specific slot it wants. Once it holds the fine-grained lock on a slot, the engine grants itself that slot (recording its identity in the slot's allocation record) and immediately releases the fine-grained lock, keeping the coarse pool lock a little longer. When an engine has finished granting itself a slot it releases the coarse pool lock, which lets the other engine begin its own coarse-then-fine acquisition sequence. Each engine only ever needs one slot for the current opening auction and, once served, retires from further activity. The full set of actions is: an engine acquiring the coarse pool lock while idle; an engine that holds the coarse lock acquiring the fine-grained lock on some unclaimed slot; an engine that holds a slot's fine-grained lock granting itself that slot (updating the slot's allocation record and releasing the fine lock); and an engine that has been granted a slot releasing the coarse pool lock and retiring. SAFETY PROPERTY: For every slot in the shared pool, the set of engines that have ever been granted that slot never contains two different engines -- the coarse-then-fine locking discipline never lets both auction engines believe they own the same slot in the shared pool. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every auction engine that starts trying to acquire a slot from the shared pool eventually gets granted a slot and retires, even though the two engines must serialize through the same coarse pool lock.

---- MODULE W4Od16m2p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants

\* A two-phase-commit coordinator decides whether any dispensing cabinet
\* (Participants) may perform the irreversible physical dispense of a
\* single controlled-substance prescription. A privileged pharmacist may
\* force the coordinator's decision before it is made, but once committed
\* or aborted the decision is final. The invariant protects the fact that
\* the irreversible dispense never happens at two different cabinets.

VARIABLES coordState, votes, dispensed, adminUsed

TypeOK ==
  /\ coordState \in {"init", "preparing", "committed", "aborted"}
  /\ votes \in [Participants -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
  /\ dispensed \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ adminUsed \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ coordState = "init"
  /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
  /\ dispensed = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
  /\ adminUsed = FALSE

StartPrepare ==
  /\ coordState = "init"
  /\ coordState' = "preparing"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dispensed, adminUsed>>

Vote(p) ==
  /\ coordState = "preparing"
  /\ votes[p] = "none"
  /\ \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coordState, dispensed, adminUsed>>

Commit ==
  /\ coordState = "preparing"
  /\ \A p \in Participants : votes[p] = "yes"
  /\ coordState' = "committed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dispensed, adminUsed>>

Abort ==
  /\ coordState = "preparing"
  /\ \E p \in Participants : votes[p] = "no"
  /\ coordState' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dispensed, adminUsed>>

Dispense(p) ==
  /\ coordState = "committed"
  /\ ~dispensed[p]
  /\ \A q \in Participants : ~dispensed[q]
  /\ dispensed' = [dispensed EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coordState, votes, adminUsed>>

AdminForceCommit ==
  /\ coordState \in {"init", "preparing"}
  /\ coordState' = "committed"
  /\ adminUsed' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dispensed>>

AdminForceAbort ==
  /\ coordState \in {"init", "preparing"}
  /\ coordState' = "aborted"
  /\ adminUsed' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dispensed>>

Next ==
  \/ StartPrepare
  \/ (\E p \in Participants : Vote(p))
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ (\E p \in Participants : Dispense(p))
  \/ AdminForceCommit
  \/ AdminForceAbort

vars == <<coordState, votes, dispensed, adminUsed>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: no two distinct cabinets ever both record having dispensed.
AtMostOnceDispensed ==
  \A p, q \in Participants : (dispensed[p] /\ dispensed[q]) => p = q

nl: A hospital pharmacy coordinates several automated dispensing cabinets, one per ward, that all could physically dispense a single controlled-substance prescription. Because the physical act of dispensing the medication is irreversible (the pill cannot be put back), the pharmacy's dispensing coordinator uses a two-phase commit protocol across the cabinets before any of them is allowed to dispense: the coordinator first asks every cabinet to prepare, each cabinet independently votes yes (it can safely dispense) or no (it cannot), and the coordinator commits only if every cabinet voted yes, or aborts if any cabinet voted no. Only once the coordinator has committed may a cabinet actually perform the physical dispense, and it must first double-check that no cabinet anywhere in the system has already dispensed this prescription before doing so itself. Separately, the pharmacy's on-duty pharmacist holds a privileged override: while the coordinator is still in its initial or preparing phase (before any commit or abort decision has been recorded), the pharmacist may force the coordinator directly to a committed or aborted decision, bypassing the normal vote collection, for example to fast-track an urgent prescription or shut down a suspicious one. Once the coordinator has reached a committed or aborted decision, that decision is final and cannot be overridden or reversed. The full set of actions is: the coordinator moving from its initial state into the preparing phase; a cabinet that has not yet voted casting a yes or no vote while the coordinator is preparing; the coordinator committing once every cabinet has voted yes; the coordinator aborting once at least one cabinet has voted no; a cabinet dispensing the prescription once the coordinator has committed and no cabinet anywhere has dispensed yet; the pharmacist force-committing the decision from the initial or preparing phase; and the pharmacist force-aborting the decision from the initial or preparing phase. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for any two dispensing cabinets that have both recorded themselves as having dispensed this prescription, they must in fact be the same cabinet -- the irreversible dispense action never happens at more than one cabinet for the same prescription.

---- MODULE W4Od16m7p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Prescriptions, MaxSlots, MinCap

\* A pharmacy dispenser bin is claimed via an optimistic compare-and-swap
\* register (a per-bin version counter) instead of a hard lock: a controller
\* reads a bin's version, then commits only if it still matches. Usable
\* capacity (how many of the MaxSlots physical bins are in service) can be
\* expanded or retired at runtime by pharmacy operations. The invariant
\* protects against two prescriptions ever holding a live claim on one bin.
VARIABLES capacity, alloc, version, pending, inflight, done

Init ==
    /\ capacity = MinCap
    /\ alloc = {}
    /\ version = [s \in 1..MaxSlots |-> 0]
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ done = {}

IsActive(p) ==
    \/ p \in pending
    \/ p \in done
    \/ \E s \in 1..MaxSlots : <<p, s>> \in alloc
    \/ \E t \in inflight : t[1] = p

Submit(p) ==
    /\ ~IsActive(p)
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, alloc, version, inflight, done>>

ReadForCAS(p) ==
    /\ p \in pending
    /\ \E s \in 1..capacity :
         /\ \A q \in Prescriptions : <<q, s>> \notin alloc
         /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {<<p, s, version[s]>>}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, alloc, version, done>>

CommitClaim(p) ==
    \E t \in inflight :
        /\ t[1] = p
        /\ version[t[2]] = t[3]
        /\ alloc' = alloc \cup {<<p, t[2]>>}
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![t[2]] = @ + 1]
        /\ inflight' = inflight \ {t}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, pending, done>>

FailRetry(p) ==
    \E t \in inflight :
        /\ t[1] = p
        /\ version[t[2]] # t[3]
        /\ pending' = pending \cup {p}
        /\ inflight' = inflight \ {t}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, alloc, version, done>>

Dispense(p) ==
    \E s \in 1..MaxSlots :
        /\ <<p, s>> \in alloc
        /\ alloc' = alloc \ {<<p, s>>}
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
        /\ done' = done \cup {p}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, pending, inflight>>

ExpandCapacity ==
    /\ capacity < MaxSlots
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, version, pending, inflight, done>>

RetireCapacity ==
    /\ capacity > MinCap
    /\ \A p \in Prescriptions : <<p, capacity>> \notin alloc
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, version, pending, inflight, done>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : Submit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : ReadForCAS(p)
    \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : CommitClaim(p)
    \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : FailRetry(p)
    \/ \E p \in Prescriptions : Dispense(p)
    \/ ExpandCapacity
    \/ RetireCapacity

vars == <<capacity, alloc, version, pending, inflight, done>>

Fairness ==
    \A p \in Prescriptions :
        /\ WF_vars(Submit(p))
        /\ WF_vars(ReadForCAS(p))
        /\ WF_vars(CommitClaim(p))
        /\ WF_vars(FailRetry(p))
        /\ WF_vars(Dispense(p))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the occupancy relation is (at most) a partial function slot -> prescription.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A p1, p2 \in Prescriptions, s \in 1..MaxSlots :
        (<<p1, s>> \in alloc /\ <<p2, s>> \in alloc) => p1 = p2

AllDispensed == <>(done = Prescriptions)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Prescriptions = {p1, p2, p3}
    MaxSlots = 2
    MinCap = 1
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY AllDispensed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs an automated prescription dispenser with a bank of physical dispensing bins. Each bin can hold exactly one prescription bag at a time. Instead of a hard lock, the dispenser controller software claims a bin using a compare-and-swap (CAS) style optimistic register: each bin has a version counter, and a controller that wants to fill a bin first takes an optimistic read of the bin's current version, then later tries to commit its claim only if the bin's version has not changed since that read. If another controller claimed (or released) the bin in the meantime, the version will have moved and the CAS commit must fail, forcing the controller to retry with a fresh read. The twist is that the pharmacy's operations team can add or retire dispensing bins while the system is running (e.g. bringing a bin back online after cleaning, or taking one out of service for restocking), so the number of usable bins changes at runtime, though it never drops to zero.

The full set of actions is:
1. Submit: a not-yet-active prescription is registered as pending, waiting to be placed into a bin.
2. OpticalRead (read-for-CAS): a pending prescription's controller picks a currently-appearing-empty bin (whose index is within the current usable-capacity range) and records an in-flight CAS attempt capturing that bin's version at read time.
3. CommitClaim: an in-flight attempt commits successfully only if the bin's version still equals the version captured at read time; on success the prescription becomes the recorded occupant of that bin and the bin's version is bumped.
4. FailRetry: an in-flight attempt whose captured version no longer matches the bin's current version is discarded and the prescription goes back to pending to try again.
5. Dispense: a prescription currently occupying a bin is handed to the patient; the bin's occupancy record for that prescription is cleared, the bin's version is bumped, and the prescription is marked done.
6. ExpandCapacity: operations brings one more bin into service, increasing the usable-capacity count (bounded by the physical number of bins installed).
7. RetireCapacity: operations takes the highest-indexed usable bin out of service, decreasing the usable-capacity count, but only when that bin is not currently occupied, and never below one usable bin.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for any two prescriptions recorded as currently occupying the same bin, they must in fact be the same prescription -- i.e. the occupancy relation never lets two distinct prescriptions both hold a claim on one bin at once, even as capacity is expanded or retired at runtime.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prescription that is ever submitted is eventually dispensed to the patient, despite bins being optimistically (and sometimes unsuccessfully) claimed via CAS retries and despite the number of usable bins changing over time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m5p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Admin, Slots, Bags, Quorum, NoBag

\* An airport baggage router: several routing controllers nominate a bag for
\* a physical conveyor slot and gather yes-votes from the non-admin voting
\* pool; a slot is only handed to a bag once a quorum of controllers agrees.
\* A single privileged Admin controller may force-assign (or reassign) a
\* slot immediately, but doing so atomically evicts any current holder and
\* clears any in-flight vote so an override can never coexist with a
\* quorum commit for the same slot.
\* The invariant guards the physical fact that a slot can never be recorded
\* as simultaneously holding two different bags.

VARIABLES proposal, votes, allocated, overridden

TypeOK ==
  /\ proposal \in [Slots -> Bags \cup {NoBag}]
  /\ votes \in [Slots -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ allocated \subseteq (Slots \times Bags)
  /\ overridden \subseteq Slots

Init ==
  /\ proposal = [s \in Slots |-> NoBag]
  /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
  /\ allocated = {}
  /\ overridden = {}

SlotHolders(s) == {b \in Bags : <<s, b>> \in allocated}

Nominate(s, b) ==
  /\ proposal[s] = NoBag
  /\ SlotHolders(s) = {}
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = b]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, overridden>>

CastVote(c, s) ==
  /\ c \in Controllers \ {Admin}
  /\ proposal[s] # NoBag
  /\ c \notin votes[s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, allocated, overridden>>

Commit(s) ==
  /\ proposal[s] # NoBag
  /\ Cardinality(votes[s]) >= Quorum
  /\ SlotHolders(s) = {}
  /\ allocated' = allocated \cup {<<s, proposal[s]>>}
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = NoBag]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED overridden

Override(s, b) ==
  /\ allocated' = (allocated \ {<<s, x>> : x \in SlotHolders(s)}) \cup {<<s, b>>}
  /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = NoBag]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ overridden' = overridden \cup {s}

Release(s) ==
  /\ SlotHolders(s) # {}
  /\ allocated' = allocated \ {<<s, b>> : b \in SlotHolders(s)}
  /\ overridden' = overridden \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Bags : Nominate(s, b)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, s \in Slots : CastVote(c, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Commit(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Bags : Override(s, b)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)

vars == <<proposal, votes, allocated, overridden>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slots, b1, b2 \in Bags :
    (<<s, b1>> \in allocated /\ <<s, b2>> \in allocated) => b1 = b2

====
nl:
An airport's baggage routing system directs suitcases from check-in onto a small set of physical conveyor slots that feed the sorting carousels. Several independent routing controllers cooperate to decide which bag goes onto which slot, using quorum voting on every allocation decision: a controller first nominates a bag for a free slot, then a pool of voting controllers (every controller except the privileged admin controller) casts yes-votes for that nomination. Only once the number of yes-votes for a slot's current nomination reaches the configured quorum threshold is the allocation actually committed, at which point the bag is recorded as occupying that slot. A slot can only be nominated for a new bag while it is not already holding one, and a nomination can only be committed while the slot is still free, so ordinary quorum-driven routing never lets two different bags land on the same slot at once.

The twist is that the system also has a privileged admin override: the admin controller can force-assign (or force-reassign) any slot to any bag at any time, bypassing the voting process entirely, for example to resolve a stuck vote or handle an emergency re-route. Because this override happens outside the normal quorum protocol, it atomically evicts whichever bag currently occupies the slot (if any) and clears any pending nomination and votes for that slot in the same step, so the override can never race with, or coexist with, an in-progress quorum commit for that slot. Finally, once a bag has physically left the conveyor slot, the slot is released: its allocation record is cleared (and any admin-override marker on it is cleared too), making the slot free again for a fresh nomination.

The full set of actions is: (1) Nominate a free slot for a bag, starting a fresh vote with no votes cast yet; (2) a non-admin controller casts a yes-vote for a slot's current nomination; (3) commit a slot's nomination once its yes-votes reach the quorum threshold and the slot is still free, recording the bag as occupying the slot; (4) the admin controller force-assigns/reassigns a slot to a bag, evicting any current occupant and clearing any pending nomination/votes for that slot; (5) release a slot once its bag departs, clearing its allocation record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for every physical slot, if two bags are both recorded as occupying that slot, they must in fact be the same bag -- i.e. no slot is ever simultaneously double-allocated to two distinct bags, whether the allocation came from a quorum commit or from the admin override.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m8p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Integers

CONSTANTS Zones, Bags, NoneZ, MaxWork, VersionModulus

\* Zone controllers update per-bag routing records through a hierarchical
\* reservation discipline: a coarse reservation on the shared corridor,
\* then a fine reservation on one bag's record. A controller may be
\* arbitrarily (but finitely) slow while it holds the fine reservation --
\* it is never treated as failed, so the corridor and the bag simply wait.
\* The invariant protects that no update ever slips past a held reservation.

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, status, workLeft, version, seenVersion

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarseLock \in Zones \cup {NoneZ}
  /\ fineLock \in [Bags -> Zones \cup {NoneZ}]
  /\ status \in [Zones -> {"idle", "coarse", "fine", "done"}]
  /\ workLeft \in [Zones -> 0..MaxWork]
  /\ version \in [Bags -> 0..(VersionModulus - 1)]
  /\ seenVersion \in [Zones -> 0..(VersionModulus - 1)]

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = NoneZ
  /\ fineLock = [b \in Bags |-> NoneZ]
  /\ status = [z \in Zones |-> "idle"]
  /\ workLeft = [z \in Zones |-> 0]
  /\ version = [b \in Bags |-> 0]
  /\ seenVersion = [z \in Zones |-> 0]

AcquireCoarse(z) ==
  /\ status[z] = "idle"
  /\ coarseLock = NoneZ
  /\ coarseLock' = z
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![z] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, workLeft, version, seenVersion>>

AcquireFine(z, b) ==
  /\ status[z] = "coarse"
  /\ coarseLock = z
  /\ fineLock[b] = NoneZ
  /\ \E w \in 0..MaxWork :
       /\ workLeft' = [workLeft EXCEPT ![z] = w]
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![b] = z]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![z] = "fine"]
  /\ seenVersion' = [seenVersion EXCEPT ![z] = version[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, version>>

Grind(z) ==
  /\ status[z] = "fine"
  /\ workLeft[z] > 0
  /\ workLeft' = [workLeft EXCEPT ![z] = workLeft[z] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, status, version, seenVersion>>

Commit(z, b) ==
  /\ status[z] = "fine"
  /\ fineLock[b] = z
  /\ workLeft[z] = 0
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = (version[b] + 1) % VersionModulus]
  /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![b] = NoneZ]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![z] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, workLeft, seenVersion>>

ReleaseCoarse(z) ==
  /\ status[z] = "done"
  /\ coarseLock = z
  /\ coarseLock' = NoneZ
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![z] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, workLeft, version, seenVersion>>

Next ==
  \/ (\E z \in Zones : AcquireCoarse(z))
  \/ (\E z \in Zones, b \in Bags : AcquireFine(z, b))
  \/ (\E z \in Zones : Grind(z))
  \/ (\E z \in Zones, b \in Bags : Commit(z, b))
  \/ (\E z \in Zones : ReleaseCoarse(z))

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, status, workLeft, version, seenVersion>>

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A z \in Zones : WF_vars(AcquireCoarse(z))
  /\ \A z \in Zones : WF_vars(\E b \in Bags : AcquireFine(z, b))
  /\ \A z \in Zones : WF_vars(Grind(z))
  /\ \A z \in Zones : WF_vars(\E b \in Bags : Commit(z, b))
  /\ \A z \in Zones : WF_vars(ReleaseCoarse(z))

\* Safety: while a zone holds a bag's fine-grained reservation, that bag's
\* version still matches exactly what the zone observed on acquiring it --
\* no concurrent write has slipped in and been lost underneath the holder.
NoLostUpdates ==
  \A z \in Zones : \A b \in Bags :
    (status[z] = "fine" /\ fineLock[b] = z) => version[b] = seenVersion[z]

EventualCommit == \A z \in Zones : (status[z] = "fine" ~> status[z] = "done")

====
