SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Zones = {z1, z2}
    Bags = {b1, b2}
    NoneZ = none
    MaxWork = 1
    VersionModulus = 2
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY EventualCommit
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: An airport baggage router moves bags through a physical sortation corridor that is shared by several zone controllers. Each bag has a shared routing record consisting of a version counter that must be bumped every time some zone controller updates it. To update a bag's record, a zone controller must first reserve the whole corridor with a coarse-grained reservation (so no other zone controller's bookkeeping interleaves with its own at the corridor level), and only then take a fine-grained reservation on the one specific bag record it intends to update; while it holds that reservation no other zone controller may touch the same bag's record, which is what stops an update from ever being silently lost or overwritten. When a zone controller takes the fine-grained reservation on a bag it also remembers the version number it currently sees on that record. The controller performing the update is allowed to be slow: after taking the fine-grained reservation it may spend an unpredictable, but always finite, number of extra turns still working on the bag (for example, waiting on a barcode rescan) before it is ready to commit -- the corridor and the bag record simply wait for it, and the system never treats a merely-slow controller as failed or takes the reservation away from it. Once it is finally ready, the controller commits by bumping the bag's version counter and immediately releasing the fine-grained reservation on that bag, while continuing to hold the corridor reservation a little longer. Only after committing does it release the corridor reservation, which frees the corridor for another zone controller's coarse-then-fine sequence. The full set of actions is: a zone controller reserving the shared corridor while idle; a zone controller that holds the corridor reserving one specific bag's record (recording the version it currently observes and picking how many extra turns of work it will still need); a zone controller that is still working spending one more turn of work; a zone controller that has finished working committing its update (bumping the bag's version counter and releasing the bag's fine-grained reservation); and a zone controller releasing the corridor reservation after committing. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for any zone controller that currently holds a bag's fine-grained reservation, that bag's version counter still equals exactly the version the controller observed when it took the reservation -- no other update has slipped in underneath it and been lost. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every zone controller that takes a fine-grained reservation on a bag eventually finishes its work and commits its update, no matter how many extra turns of slow work it needs first.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m2p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Branches, HomeBranch, Total, NoBranch

\* A library system tracks a fixed number of physical copies of one title
\* across several branches. A copy is always in exactly one of: on a
\* branch's shelf, reserved (held for a patron's pickup), checked out
\* (on loan), or mid-transfer between two branches. Inter-branch transfers
\* use two-phase commit: a Prepare debits the source shelf and parks the
\* copy "in transit", and only a later Commit credits the destination (or
\* an Abort returns it to the source). A privileged admin may also force
\* an immediate single-step transfer between two branches, bypassing the
\* prepare/commit protocol entirely.
\* The invariant protects conservation: summed across every bucket and
\* every branch, copies are never created or destroyed by any action.

RECURSIVE SumF(_, _)
SumF(S, f) == IF S = {} THEN 0 ELSE
                LET x == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE
                IN f[x] + SumF(S \ {x}, f)

VARIABLES shelf, reserved, checkedOut, inTransit

TypeOK ==
  /\ shelf \in [Branches -> 0..Total]
  /\ reserved \in [Branches -> 0..Total]
  /\ checkedOut \in [Branches -> 0..Total]
  /\ inTransit \in [Branches \X Branches -> 0..Total]

Init ==
  /\ shelf = [br \in Branches |-> IF br = HomeBranch THEN Total ELSE 0]
  /\ reserved = [br \in Branches |-> 0]
  /\ checkedOut = [br \in Branches |-> 0]
  /\ inTransit = [p \in Branches \X Branches |-> 0]

Reserve(br) ==
  /\ shelf[br] > 0
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![br] = @ - 1]
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![br] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<checkedOut, inTransit>>

CancelReservation(br) ==
  /\ reserved[br] > 0
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![br] = @ - 1]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![br] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<checkedOut, inTransit>>

CheckOut(br) ==
  /\ reserved[br] > 0
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![br] = @ - 1]
  /\ checkedOut' = [checkedOut EXCEPT ![br] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, inTransit>>

Return(br) ==
  /\ checkedOut[br] > 0
  /\ checkedOut' = [checkedOut EXCEPT ![br] = @ - 1]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![br] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, inTransit>>

PrepareTransfer(src, dst) ==
  /\ src # dst
  /\ shelf[src] > 0
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![src] = @ - 1]
  /\ inTransit' = [inTransit EXCEPT ![<<src, dst>>] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, checkedOut>>

CommitTransfer(src, dst) ==
  /\ inTransit[<<src, dst>>] > 0
  /\ inTransit' = [inTransit EXCEPT ![<<src, dst>>] = @ - 1]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![dst] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, checkedOut>>

AbortTransfer(src, dst) ==
  /\ inTransit[<<src, dst>>] > 0
  /\ inTransit' = [inTransit EXCEPT ![<<src, dst>>] = @ - 1]
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![src] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, checkedOut>>

AdminTransfer(src, dst) ==
  /\ src # dst
  /\ shelf[src] > 0
  /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![src] = @ - 1, ![dst] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, checkedOut, inTransit>>

Next ==
  \/ \E br \in Branches : Reserve(br)
  \/ \E br \in Branches : CancelReservation(br)
  \/ \E br \in Branches : CheckOut(br)
  \/ \E br \in Branches : Return(br)
  \/ \E src, dst \in Branches : PrepareTransfer(src, dst)
  \/ \E src, dst \in Branches : CommitTransfer(src, dst)
  \/ \E src, dst \in Branches : AbortTransfer(src, dst)
  \/ \E src, dst \in Branches : AdminTransfer(src, dst)

vars == <<shelf, reserved, checkedOut, inTransit>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ConservedTotal ==
  SumF(Branches, shelf) + SumF(Branches, reserved) + SumF(Branches, checkedOut)
    + SumF(Branches \X Branches, inTransit) = Total

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Branches = {br1, br2, br3}
    HomeBranch = br1
    Total = 3
    NoBranch = nobranch
INVARIANT ConservedTotal
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A library system tracks a fixed number of physical copies of one book title spread across several branches. At any moment, every copy is in exactly one of four states: sitting on a branch's shelf available to browse, reserved and held for a patron waiting to pick it up at a branch, checked out on loan from a branch, or in transit between two branches as part of an inter-branch transfer. Transfers between branches are coordinated with two-phase commit across the participating branches: a transfer first prepares by debiting one copy from the source branch's shelf and parking it in an in-transit bucket for that specific source/destination route, and only later does a second, separate step either commit the transfer (crediting the copy to the destination branch's shelf) or abort it (returning the copy to the source branch's shelf) -- the copy sits in transit, belonging to neither branch's shelf, for as long as the transfer is undecided. On top of the normal two-phase protocol, a privileged system administrator can also force an immediate, single-step transfer of one shelf copy directly from one branch to another, bypassing the prepare/commit/abort protocol entirely (for example, to fix a stuck or lost transfer without waiting for the normal decision step).

The full set of actions is: (1) reserve an available shelf copy at a branch for a patron, moving it from that branch's shelf into that branch's reserved bucket; (2) cancel a reservation at a branch, moving a copy back from reserved to that branch's shelf; (3) check out a reserved copy at a branch, moving it from reserved into that branch's checked-out bucket; (4) return a checked-out copy at a branch, moving it from checked-out back onto that branch's shelf; (5) prepare an inter-branch transfer from a source branch to a destination branch, debiting one copy from the source branch's shelf into the in-transit bucket for that source/destination pair; (6) commit a prepared transfer for a source/destination pair, moving its in-transit copy onto the destination branch's shelf; (7) abort a prepared transfer for a source/destination pair, returning its in-transit copy to the source branch's shelf; (8) the admin force-transfers one shelf copy directly from a source branch to a destination branch in a single step, bypassing the prepare/commit/abort protocol.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the sum of every copy currently on a shelf, reserved, checked out, or in transit between any pair of branches equals the fixed total number of copies of the title the library system started with -- no action, including the admin's override, ever creates or destroys a copy.

---- MODULE W4Od19m3p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT Servers, InitLeader, Books, AdminS, NoneS, NoneW, MaxTerm

\* Leader election with failover: a crashed leader is replaced by a surviving
\* server in a new term, and may later recover to crash again. The admin
\* override is a privileged bypass path that can perform the irreversible
\* write-off independent of leader/crash state. The invariant protects the
\* fact that the two paths (leader, admin) can never both succeed on one book.

VARIABLES leader, term, crashedS, requested, writeOffBy, writeOffCount

vars == <<leader, term, crashedS, requested, writeOffBy, writeOffCount>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Servers
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ crashedS \in Servers \cup {NoneS}
    /\ requested \in [Books -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ writeOffBy \in [Books -> Servers \cup {AdminS, NoneW}]
    /\ writeOffCount \in [Books -> 0..1]

Init ==
    /\ leader = InitLeader
    /\ term = 0
    /\ crashedS = NoneS
    /\ requested = [b \in Books |-> FALSE]
    /\ writeOffBy = [b \in Books |-> NoneW]
    /\ writeOffCount = [b \in Books |-> 0]

Crash ==
    /\ crashedS = NoneS
    /\ crashedS' = leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, requested, writeOffBy, writeOffCount>>

Failover ==
    /\ crashedS # NoneS
    /\ leader = crashedS
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ \E s \in Servers \ {crashedS} : leader' = s
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashedS, requested, writeOffBy, writeOffCount>>

Recover ==
    /\ crashedS # NoneS
    /\ leader # crashedS
    /\ crashedS' = NoneS
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, requested, writeOffBy, writeOffCount>>

RequestWriteOff(b) ==
    /\ ~requested[b]
    /\ requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedS, writeOffBy, writeOffCount>>

LeaderWriteOff(b) ==
    /\ requested[b]
    /\ writeOffBy[b] = NoneW
    /\ leader # crashedS
    /\ writeOffBy' = [writeOffBy EXCEPT ![b] = leader]
    /\ writeOffCount' = [writeOffCount EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedS, requested>>

AdminOverride(b) ==
    /\ requested[b]
    /\ writeOffBy[b] = NoneW
    /\ writeOffBy' = [writeOffBy EXCEPT ![b] = AdminS]
    /\ writeOffCount' = [writeOffCount EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedS, requested>>

Next ==
    \/ Crash
    \/ Failover
    \/ Recover
    \/ \E b \in Books : RequestWriteOff(b) \/ LeaderWriteOff(b) \/ AdminOverride(b)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Failover)
    /\ WF_vars(Recover)
    /\ \A b \in Books : WF_vars(LeaderWriteOff(b)) /\ WF_vars(AdminOverride(b))

\* At most once: no book's irreversible write-off is ever executed twice,
\* whether by successive leaders across failovers or by the admin override.
AtMostOnceWriteOff == \A b \in Books : writeOffCount[b] <= 1

EventuallyWrittenOff == \A b \in Books : requested[b] ~> (writeOffBy[b] # NoneW)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Servers = {S1, S2, S3}
    InitLeader = S1
    Books = {B1, B2, B3}
    AdminS = AdminS
    NoneS = NoneS
    NoneW = NoneW
    MaxTerm = 2
INVARIANT AtMostOnceWriteOff
PROPERTY EventuallyWrittenOff
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A library's book-reservation backend runs on a small cluster of servers, one of which is the elected leader responsible for processing catalog write-offs -- the irreversible act of permanently removing a lost or damaged book from the reservable catalog once it has been reported missing. The leader can crash at any time; when it does, a surviving server is elected as the new leader in a new term, and the crashed server may later rejoin the cluster and become eligible to crash again in some future term. Separately, a privileged library administrator holds an override that lets them force a write-off directly at any time, bypassing the leader entirely -- even while a leader election is in progress or the current leader is down -- as long as the book has been reported and has not already been written off by anyone.

The full set of actions is:
1. Crash: the current leader crashes (only possible if no server is currently down).
2. Failover: once the leader has crashed, a surviving server is elected the new leader and the term counter increases.
3. Recover: a previously crashed server (which is no longer the leader, having been replaced by failover) rejoins the cluster and becomes eligible to crash again later.
4. RequestWriteOff(b): a book b that has not yet been reported is reported missing.
5. LeaderWriteOff(b): the current leader, provided it is not itself the currently-crashed server, permanently writes off a reported book that has not yet been written off.
6. AdminOverride(b): the admin permanently writes off a reported book that has not yet been written off, regardless of the leader's or the cluster's current state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every book, the irreversible write-off action is executed at most once in total, whether it is ultimately performed by whichever server happens to be leader or by the admin's override -- the two paths can never both succeed for the same book.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every book that is ever reported missing is eventually permanently written off by either the leader or the admin, no matter how many times the leader crashes and fails over in the meantime.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Capacity, MaxRetries, MaxVersion, NoVal

\* A warehouse robot fleet shares a bounded set of charging-dock slots. A
\* robot reserves a slot using optimistic concurrency: it reads the current
\* version stamp, and its reservation commits only if the stamp is still
\* current at commit time and a slot is actually free; otherwise the
\* snapshot is stale and the robot retries. A privileged admin can force a
\* robot straight into a slot without going through the optimistic
\* read/retry dance at all -- but the admin path still has to respect the
\* dock's physical capacity, since skipping the concurrency protocol is not
\* the same as skipping the room limit.

VARIABLES occupancy, version, readVersion, retries

TypeOK ==
    /\ occupancy \subseteq Robots
    /\ version \in Nat
    /\ readVersion \in [Robots -> Nat \cup {NoVal}]
    /\ retries \in [Robots -> Nat]

Init ==
    /\ occupancy = {}
    /\ version = 0
    /\ readVersion = [r \in Robots |-> NoVal]
    /\ retries = [r \in Robots |-> 0]

\* A robot not currently docked and not already mid-attempt takes a snapshot
\* of the current version stamp before trying to reserve a slot.
ReadSnapshot(r) ==
    /\ r \notin occupancy
    /\ readVersion[r] = NoVal
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![r] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, version, retries>>

\* The optimistic commit: it only succeeds if nothing has changed since the
\* robot's snapshot was taken AND a dock slot is actually free.
CommitReserve(r) ==
    /\ readVersion[r] # NoVal
    /\ readVersion[r] = version
    /\ Cardinality(occupancy) < Capacity
    /\ occupancy' = occupancy \cup {r}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![r] = NoVal]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

\* If the world moved on since the robot's snapshot, the attempt is stale;
\* the robot drops it and (bounded) retries by taking a fresh snapshot later.
AbortAndRetry(r) ==
    /\ readVersion[r] # NoVal
    /\ readVersion[r] # version
    /\ retries[r] < MaxRetries
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![r] = NoVal]
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, version>>

\* Admin override: skips the read/version-check/retry protocol entirely, but
\* is still bound by the same capacity check as an ordinary commit.
AdminOverride(r) ==
    /\ r \notin occupancy
    /\ Cardinality(occupancy) < Capacity
    /\ occupancy' = occupancy \cup {r}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![r] = NoVal]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

\* A docked robot finishes and leaves, freeing a slot and invalidating any
\* outstanding snapshots taken before it left.
Vacate(r) ==
    /\ r \in occupancy
    /\ occupancy' = occupancy \ {r}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readVersion, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : ReadSnapshot(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : CommitReserve(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : AbortAndRetry(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : AdminOverride(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Vacate(r)

vars == <<occupancy, version, readVersion, retries>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounds the version stamp so the reachable state space stays finite; it
\* does not restrict which actions are semantically allowed.
VersionBound == version <= MaxVersion

\* The dock's physical capacity is never exceeded, whether a robot got its
\* slot through the ordinary optimistic-commit path or through the
\* privileged admin override.
BoundedCapacity == Cardinality(occupancy) <= Capacity

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxRetries = 2
    MaxVersion = 6
    NoVal = NoVal
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
CONSTRAINT VersionBound
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a small bank of charging-dock slots with a fixed physical capacity. A robot that wants to dock uses optimistic concurrency control: it first reads a snapshot of the dock's current version stamp, and later tries to commit its reservation, which succeeds only if the version stamp is still the same one it originally read (nothing else changed the dock state in the meantime) and a slot is actually free at that moment. If the version stamp has moved on since the robot's snapshot, the reservation attempt is stale and the robot must retry (up to a bounded number of retries) by taking a fresh snapshot and trying again. Separately, a privileged admin can force a robot straight into a free slot without going through the read/version-check/retry protocol at all -- but this override does not let the admin exceed the dock's physical capacity; it only lets a robot skip the normal contention-resolution dance, not the room limit itself.

The full set of actions is:
1. ReadSnapshot: a robot that is not currently docked and has no attempt already in flight reads the dock's current version stamp, beginning a reservation attempt.
2. CommitReserve: a robot with an in-flight snapshot commits its reservation, which succeeds only if the version stamp it read is still current and a dock slot is free; the dock's occupancy grows by one and the version stamp advances.
3. AbortAndRetry: if a robot's in-flight snapshot has gone stale (the version stamp moved on since it was read) and the robot has not exhausted its retry budget, it discards the stale snapshot and counts a retry, so it can attempt a fresh snapshot later.
4. AdminOverride: a privileged admin directly places a robot into a free dock slot, bypassing the read/version-check/retry protocol entirely, but still only when a slot is actually free -- the dock's occupancy grows by one and the version stamp advances exactly as with an ordinary commit.
5. Vacate: a docked robot finishes charging and leaves, freeing its slot and advancing the version stamp, which invalidates any snapshot another robot had already taken.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of robots occupying a dock slot never exceeds the dock's fixed capacity, regardless of whether a robot got its slot through the ordinary optimistic-commit-with-retry path or through the privileged admin override.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Instances, Nodes, Batches, MaxTerm, NoLeader

\* A bank's interbank settlement batch processor: two independent settlement
\* coordinator instances (e.g. two data-center deployments) each run their
\* own leader election with failover, yet both draw their pending work from
\* one shared pool of settlement batches. A leader must first claim a batch
\* from the shared pool before finalizing it; claims persist across a
\* leader crash so a newly-elected leader of the same instance can resume
\* and finish work its predecessor started, instead of losing it.
\* The invariant protects the fact that finalizing a batch -- an
\* irreversible transfer of funds between banks -- is ever recorded as
\* having actually happened more than once for the same batch.

VARIABLES leader, term, claimed, finalized, finalizeLog

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in [Instances -> Nodes \cup {NoLeader}]
  /\ term \in [Instances -> 0..MaxTerm]
  /\ claimed \subseteq (Batches \times Instances)
  /\ finalized \subseteq Batches
  /\ finalizeLog \subseteq (Batches \times Instances \times (0..MaxTerm))

Init ==
  /\ leader = [i \in Instances |-> NoLeader]
  /\ term = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
  /\ claimed = {}
  /\ finalized = {}
  /\ finalizeLog = {}

Elect(i, n) ==
  /\ leader[i] = NoLeader
  /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = n]
  /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![i] = IF @ < MaxTerm THEN @ + 1 ELSE @]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, finalized, finalizeLog>>

Fail(i) ==
  /\ leader[i] # NoLeader
  /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = NoLeader]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, claimed, finalized, finalizeLog>>

Claim(i, b) ==
  /\ leader[i] # NoLeader
  /\ b \notin finalized
  /\ \A i2 \in Instances : <<b, i2>> \notin claimed
  /\ claimed' = claimed \cup {<<b, i>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, finalized, finalizeLog>>

Finalize(i, b) ==
  /\ leader[i] # NoLeader
  /\ <<b, i>> \in claimed
  /\ b \notin finalized
  /\ finalized' = finalized \cup {b}
  /\ finalizeLog' = finalizeLog \cup {<<b, i, term[i]>>}
  /\ claimed' = claimed \ {<<b, i>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

ElectFor(i)   == \E n \in Nodes : Elect(i, n)
FinalizeFor(b) == \E i \in Instances : Finalize(i, b)

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, n \in Nodes : Elect(i, n)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Fail(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Batches : Claim(i, b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Batches : Finalize(i, b)

vars == <<leader, term, claimed, finalized, finalizeLog>>

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A i \in Instances : WF_vars(ElectFor(i))
  /\ \A b \in Batches : SF_vars(FinalizeFor(b))

AtMostOnceFinalized ==
  \A b \in Batches : Cardinality({r \in finalizeLog : r[1] = b}) <= 1

BatchEventuallyFinalized ==
  \A b \in Batches : (\E i \in Instances : <<b, i>> \in claimed) ~> (b \in finalized)

====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement system processes batches of transfers between banks. Two independent settlement-coordinator instances -- for example, deployments running in two separate data centers -- each run their own leader election with failover, but both instances draw their pending work from one shared pool of settlement batches rather than each owning a private slice of it. Only the currently-elected leader of an instance may act on that instance's behalf. Before a leader can finalize a batch (irreversibly commit the fund transfers it represents to the interbank ledger), it must first claim that batch from the shared pool; a claim can only be taken on a batch that is not already finalized and that no instance (including its own) currently holds a claim on. Crucially, a claim survives its leader crashing: if a leader fails mid-processing, the claim it holds is not released, so once a new leader is elected for that same instance, the new leader can pick up exactly where its predecessor left off and finalize the still-claimed batch, rather than the work being lost or having to restart from scratch.

The full action set is: (1) elect a new leader for an instance that currently has none, choosing any candidate node and bumping that instance's term counter (saturating once it reaches the configured maximum term, so re-election always stays possible); (2) the current leader of an instance fails/crashes, leaving that instance leaderless (any claims it holds remain intact); (3) the current leader of an instance claims an unfinalized batch from the shared pool, provided no instance already holds a claim on it; (4) the current leader of an instance finalizes a batch it holds a claim on that is not yet finalized, irreversibly recording the transfer as committed (tagged with the instance and the leader's current term) and releasing the claim.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for every settlement batch, the ghost record of every finalize event that has ever actually occurred for that batch contains at most one entry -- i.e. a batch's irreversible fund transfer is committed at most once, even though two independent coordinator instances both race to claim and finalize batches out of the very same shared pool.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every settlement batch that is ever claimed by either coordinator instance is eventually finalized, even though the claiming instance's leader may crash partway through and have to be replaced by a newly-elected leader before the work can be completed.

---- MODULE W4Od3m5p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Quorum, NoBank, MaxClock

\* Banks in an interbank settlement batch must take turns holding exclusive
\* access to the shared settlement ledger (the critical resource) so that
\* net positions are computed without interference. Access is granted not by
\* a lock but by quorum voting: a requester needs pledges from enough banks
\* (Quorum of them, counting itself) before it may enter. Because a bank can
\* be slow to respond but never fails outright, a pledge it is still sitting
\* on can be reclaimed by an older, higher-priority request (Preempt) so that
\* a slow voter can never permanently stall someone else's progress.

VARIABLES pc, ts, clock, votedFor, votes

TypeOK ==
    /\ pc \in [Banks -> {"idle", "reqing", "holding"}]
    /\ ts \in [Banks -> Nat]
    /\ clock \in Nat
    /\ votedFor \in [Banks -> Banks \cup {NoBank}]
    /\ votes \in [Banks -> SUBSET Banks]

Init ==
    /\ pc = [b \in Banks |-> "idle"]
    /\ ts = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ votedFor = [b \in Banks |-> NoBank]
    /\ votes = [b \in Banks |-> {}]

\* An idle bank asks for the ledger, stamping its request with the next tick
\* of the shared clock (older tick = higher priority) and immediately
\* pledging its own vote to itself. A bank may only start a request while its
\* own single vote-token is free, so a vote it lent out elsewhere is never
\* silently orphaned in another requester's tally.
Request(b) ==
    /\ pc[b] = "idle"
    /\ votedFor[b] = NoBank
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![b] = "reqing"]
    /\ ts' = [ts EXCEPT ![b] = clock]
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![b] = b]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {b}]

\* A currently unpledged bank v backs some requester b's bid.
CastVote(v, b) ==
    /\ votedFor[v] = NoBank
    /\ v # b
    /\ pc[b] = "reqing"
    /\ v \notin votes[b]
    /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![v] = b]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pc, ts, clock>>

\* The slow-but-not-failed twist: if v's pledge is currently sitting with a
\* requester cur that is strictly younger (later timestamp) than b, v may
\* reclaim its pledge from cur and give it to the older, higher-priority
\* request b instead -- this is what keeps a slow voter from stalling
\* everyone else forever.
Preempt(v, b) ==
    LET cur == votedFor[v] IN
    /\ cur # NoBank
    /\ cur # b
    /\ pc[b] = "reqing"
    /\ pc[cur] = "reqing"
    /\ ts[b] < ts[cur]
    /\ v \notin votes[b]
    /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![v] = b]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![cur] = @ \ {v}, ![b] = @ \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pc, ts, clock>>

\* Once a requester has collected pledges from at least Quorum banks it is
\* granted exclusive access to the ledger.
Enter(b) ==
    /\ pc[b] = "reqing"
    /\ Cardinality(votes[b]) >= Quorum
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![b] = "holding"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ts, clock, votedFor, votes>>

\* The holder finishes settlement and releases the ledger, freeing every
\* pledge that was sitting with it so those banks can help someone else next.
Release(b) ==
    /\ pc[b] = "holding"
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
    /\ votedFor' = [v \in Banks |-> IF votedFor[v] = b THEN NoBank ELSE votedFor[v]]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ts, clock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Request(b)
    \/ \E v, b \in Banks : CastVote(v, b)
    \/ \E v, b \in Banks : Preempt(v, b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Enter(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Release(b)

vars == <<pc, ts, clock, votedFor, votes>>

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(Enter(b))
    /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(Release(b))
    /\ \A v \in Banks : SF_vars(\E b \in Banks : CastVote(v, b))
    /\ \A v \in Banks : SF_vars(\E b \in Banks : Preempt(v, b))

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: at most one bank ever holds
\* exclusive access to the settlement ledger at once.
AtMostOneHolder == Cardinality({b \in Banks : pc[b] = "holding"}) <= 1

\* Every bank that is waiting for the ledger eventually gets it, despite
\* slow (but not failed) voters and despite contention from other requesters.
RequestEventuallyGranted == \A b \in Banks : (pc[b] = "reqing") ~> (pc[b] = "holding")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
    Quorum = 2
    NoBank = NoBank
    MaxClock = 3
INVARIANT AtMostOneHolder
PROPERTY RequestEventuallyGranted
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A small group of banks runs a periodic interbank settlement batch. Only one bank may hold exclusive access to the shared settlement ledger (the critical resource) at a time, so that it can compute and post net positions without another bank's concurrent writes corrupting the batch. Access is not granted by a simple lock but by quorum voting: each bank has a single pledge (vote) it can hold at any moment, and a bank that wants the ledger must collect pledges from at least a quorum of banks (counting its own) before it may enter. A participant bank can be arbitrarily slow to respond to a vote request -- it never crashes or refuses outright, it just may take a long time -- and the protocol must still make progress despite that.

The full set of actions is:
1. Request: an idle bank whose own single vote-token is currently free asks for the ledger. It stamps its request with the next tick of a shared logical clock (an older tick means higher priority) and immediately pledges its own vote to itself. (A bank whose vote-token is presently lent out to another requester must wait for that pledge to come back before it can start its own request, so a lent-out vote is never silently orphaned.)
2. CastVote: a bank whose pledge is currently free backs some other requesting bank's bid, handing that requester its pledge.
3. Preempt: if a bank's pledge is currently sitting with some requester that has a strictly later (lower-priority) timestamp than another, still-waiting requester, the bank reclaims its pledge from the lower-priority requester and gives it to the higher-priority one instead. This is what keeps a slow voter from permanently stalling an older, higher-priority request -- eventually every outstanding pledge gets sorted toward whichever pending request has been waiting longest.
4. Enter: once a requesting bank has collected pledges from at least a quorum of banks, it is granted exclusive access to the ledger.
5. Release: the bank holding the ledger finishes settlement and releases it, freeing every pledge that was sitting with it so those banks are available to help the next requester.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one bank holds exclusive access to the settlement ledger at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bank that is waiting for the ledger is eventually granted exclusive access to it, even though some voters may be arbitrarily slow to cast or reassign their pledge, as long as they are never permanently failed.

---- MODULE W4Od7m0p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT Cranes, MaxCapacity, InitCapacity, MaxVersion

\* Optimistic locking with retry: a crane snapshots (version, occupancy) and
\* only commits if the live version still matches its snapshot AND the live
\* (possibly just-changed) capacity still has room -- it never trusts a
\* cached capacity value. The invariant protects the fact that this
\* re-validate-at-commit discipline keeps occupancy within the live bound
\* even though capacity can be changed by yard operations at any time.

VARIABLES capacity, occupancy, version, craneState, readVersion, readOccupancy

vars == <<capacity, occupancy, version, craneState, readVersion, readOccupancy>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCapacity
    /\ occupancy \in 0..MaxCapacity
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ craneState \in [Cranes -> {"idle", "attempting"}]
    /\ readVersion \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ readOccupancy \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxCapacity]

Init ==
    /\ capacity = InitCapacity
    /\ occupancy = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ craneState = [c \in Cranes |-> "idle"]
    /\ readVersion = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ readOccupancy = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]

\* Yard operations may not strand already-placed containers: a new capacity
\* bound must still cover whatever is currently occupied.
ChangeCapacity ==
    /\ \E newCap \in occupancy..MaxCapacity : capacity' = newCap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, version, craneState, readVersion, readOccupancy>>

StartAttempt(c) ==
    /\ craneState[c] = "idle"
    /\ craneState' = [craneState EXCEPT ![c] = "attempting"]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ readOccupancy' = [readOccupancy EXCEPT ![c] = occupancy]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, occupancy, version>>

\* Re-checks the LIVE capacity, not readOccupancy/a cached bound -- this is
\* what keeps the twist (runtime capacity changes) from being violated.
CommitAttempt(c) ==
    /\ craneState[c] = "attempting"
    /\ version = readVersion[c]
    /\ occupancy < capacity
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ occupancy' = occupancy + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ craneState' = [craneState EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, readVersion, readOccupancy>>

RetryStale(c) ==
    /\ craneState[c] = "attempting"
    /\ version # readVersion[c]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ readOccupancy' = [readOccupancy EXCEPT ![c] = occupancy]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, occupancy, version, craneState>>

RetryFull(c) ==
    /\ craneState[c] = "attempting"
    /\ version = readVersion[c]
    /\ occupancy >= capacity
    /\ craneState' = [craneState EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, occupancy, version, readVersion, readOccupancy>>

Depart ==
    /\ occupancy > 0
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ occupancy' = occupancy - 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, craneState, readVersion, readOccupancy>>

Next ==
    \/ ChangeCapacity
    \/ Depart
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : StartAttempt(c) \/ CommitAttempt(c) \/ RetryStale(c) \/ RetryFull(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded, despite runtime capacity changes and
\* optimistic (lock-free) commits.
BoundedCapacity == occupancy <= capacity

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {C1, C2, C3}
    MaxCapacity = 2
    InitCapacity = 1
    MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard tracks how many containers currently sit in its staging area against a capacity bound that yard operations can raise or lower at runtime (for example, closing off part of the yard for maintenance, or reopening it later). Gantry cranes place containers into the staging area using an optimistic, versioned update: a crane first snapshots the current occupancy count and a version number, then later tries to commit one more container by comparing the live version against the one it snapshotted. If the version has moved (someone else committed in the meantime) the crane refreshes its snapshot and retries. If the version still matches but the yard's live, current capacity bound has no room left for one more container, the crane abandons this attempt and may start a fresh one later. Critically, the commit step always re-checks the *current* capacity, never a cached value from when the crane started -- so a capacity reduction that happens mid-attempt is still respected. Separately, containers also depart the yard from time to time, freeing up room and advancing the version counter just like a commit does.

The full set of actions is:
1. ChangeCapacity: yard operations set a new capacity bound, chosen freely within the allowed range but never below the number of containers currently occupying the staging area (operations cannot strand already-placed containers), independent of any crane's in-progress attempt.
2. StartAttempt(c): an idle crane snapshots the current version and occupancy count and moves into an in-progress attempt.
3. CommitAttempt(c): a crane with an in-progress attempt whose snapshotted version still matches the live version, and for whom the live occupancy is still below the live capacity, commits one more container -- occupancy and version both advance -- and returns to idle.
4. RetryStale(c): a crane with an in-progress attempt whose snapshotted version no longer matches the live version (someone else committed or a container departed) refreshes its snapshot and keeps trying.
5. RetryFull(c): a crane with an in-progress attempt whose snapshotted version still matches the live version, but whose live occupancy has reached the live capacity, abandons the attempt and returns to idle.
6. Depart: one container leaves the staging area, decrementing occupancy and advancing the version counter.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of containers occupying the staging area never exceeds the yard's current capacity bound, even though that bound can change at runtime and cranes commit optimistically with retries rather than holding an exclusive lock.

---- MODULE W4Od7m8p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT Cranes, NumZones, BaysPerZone, NoneC, NoneB, MaxRecord

\* Zones and Bays are derived from two size constants so that the coarse/fine
\* zone-to-bay grouping is parameterized rather than an arbitrary hardcoded map.
Zones == 1..NumZones
Bays == 1..(NumZones * BaysPerZone)
ZoneOf(b) == ((b - 1) \div BaysPerZone) + 1

\* Hierarchical locking: a crane must hold a zone's coarse lock before it can
\* take a bay's fine lock nested inside it. The invariant below protects the
\* fact that a crane's committed write is never applied on top of a manifest
\* value that changed underneath it -- i.e. no update is ever lost.
\* Cranes may be arbitrarily slow between phases (the twist) but never fail,
\* which is what the per-crane fairness conditions in Spec encode.

VARIABLES zoneLock, bayLock, manifest, snapshot, craneBay, status

vars == <<zoneLock, bayLock, manifest, snapshot, craneBay, status>>

Statuses == {"idle", "zoneHeld", "reading", "writing", "committed"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ zoneLock \in [Zones -> Cranes \cup {NoneC}]
    /\ bayLock \in [Bays -> Cranes \cup {NoneC}]
    /\ manifest \in [Bays -> 0..MaxRecord]
    /\ snapshot \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxRecord]
    /\ craneBay \in [Cranes -> Bays \cup {NoneB}]
    /\ status \in [Cranes -> Statuses]

Init ==
    /\ zoneLock = [z \in Zones |-> NoneC]
    /\ bayLock = [b \in Bays |-> NoneC]
    /\ manifest = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ snapshot = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ craneBay = [c \in Cranes |-> NoneB]
    /\ status = [c \in Cranes |-> "idle"]

AcquireZone(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "idle"
    /\ \E b \in Bays :
        /\ zoneLock[ZoneOf(b)] = NoneC
        /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![ZoneOf(b)] = c]
        /\ craneBay' = [craneBay EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "zoneHeld"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayLock, manifest, snapshot>>

AcquireBay(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "zoneHeld"
    /\ bayLock[craneBay[c]] = NoneC
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![craneBay[c]] = c]
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![c] = manifest[craneBay[c]]]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "reading"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, manifest, craneBay>>

StartWrite(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "reading"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "writing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, bayLock, manifest, snapshot, craneBay>>

CommitWrite(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "writing"
    /\ \E v \in 0..MaxRecord :
        manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![craneBay[c]] = v]
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![craneBay[c]] = NoneC]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, snapshot, craneBay>>

ReleaseZone(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "committed"
    /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![ZoneOf(craneBay[c])] = NoneC]
    /\ craneBay' = [craneBay EXCEPT ![c] = NoneB]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayLock, manifest, snapshot>>

Next == \E c \in Cranes :
    AcquireZone(c) \/ AcquireBay(c) \/ StartWrite(c) \/ CommitWrite(c) \/ ReleaseZone(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A c \in Cranes :
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireZone(c))
        /\ WF_vars(AcquireBay(c))
        /\ WF_vars(StartWrite(c))
        /\ WF_vars(CommitWrite(c))
        /\ WF_vars(ReleaseZone(c))

\* No lost updates: while a crane is mid-write, the bay's record still equals
\* exactly what the crane read when it took the fine lock -- nobody else's
\* concurrent write can have slipped in underneath it.
NoLostUpdates ==
    \A c \in Cranes : status[c] = "writing" => manifest[craneBay[c]] = snapshot[c]

CraneAlwaysReturnsIdle ==
    \A c \in Cranes : (status[c] # "idle") ~> (status[c] = "idle")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {C1, C2, C3}
    NumZones = 2
    BaysPerZone = 2
    NoneC = NoneC
    NoneB = NoneB
    MaxRecord = 1
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY CraneAlwaysReturnsIdle
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is divided into zones, and each zone contains several bays. Each bay holds a shared manifest record (the recorded container count for that bay) that traveling gantry cranes must update whenever they move containers through it. To touch a bay's record, a crane must first acquire the zone's coarse-grained lock, then acquire the bay's fine-grained lock nested inside it; only after holding both does it read the record and later commit a new value. A crane can be slow -- it may take an arbitrarily long time between reading the record and committing its new value, or between committing and releasing the coarse zone lock -- but it never crashes or abandons its locks, so it always eventually finishes its cycle.

The full set of actions is:
1. AcquireZone(c): an idle crane picks some bay, and if that bay's zone lock is free, takes the zone lock and marks itself as holding the zone.
2. AcquireBay(c): a crane holding its chosen bay's zone lock takes the bay's fine lock (if free) and immediately snapshots the bay's current manifest value into its own local reading.
3. StartWrite(c): a crane that has snapshotted the record (and may have been slow up to this point) moves to the writing phase, still holding both locks.
4. CommitWrite(c): a crane in the writing phase picks a new record value and writes it into the bay's manifest, then releases the bay's fine lock, without yet releasing the zone lock.
5. ReleaseZone(c): a crane that has committed its write releases the zone lock and returns to idle, free to start a new cycle on any bay.

Because a crane holds the bay's fine lock exclusively from the moment it snapshots the record until it commits, no other crane can modify that bay's manifest value in between -- so the update a crane commits is never silently clobbered by, or built on top of, someone else's concurrent write. The hierarchical (coarse-then-fine) locking is what makes this true even though individual cranes may dawdle for a long time between phases.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a crane is in its writing phase for a bay, that bay's manifest value still equals exactly the value the crane snapshotted when it acquired the bay's fine lock, so no update the crane is about to commit can be applied on top of a stale or concurrently-changed record.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every crane that leaves the idle state (because it started a new update cycle) eventually returns to idle having committed its record update and released both locks, even though it may be arbitrarily slow along the way, because it never fails.

---- MODULE W4Od7m8p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Instances, LocalSlots, MaxCapacity, NoneI

\* Two independent crane-yard instances share ONE storage pool of bounded
\* capacity. Admission is hierarchical: a coarse pool-wide permit must be
\* held before an instance may make a fine-grained local-slot reservation
\* and commit into the shared pool. The invariant protects the pool bound
\* as an emergent property of BOTH instances' committed placements together.
VARIABLES admission, reserved, placed, pendingReq

Init ==
    /\ admission = NoneI
    /\ reserved = [i \in Instances |-> {}]
    /\ placed = [i \in Instances |-> {}]
    /\ pendingReq = {}

\* Every container committed anywhere, tagged by which instance owns it, so
\* the pool bound is checked against BOTH instances' placements combined.
AllPlaced == UNION {{<<i, s>> : s \in placed[i]} : i \in Instances}

Request(i) ==
    /\ i \notin pendingReq
    /\ \E s \in LocalSlots : s \notin placed[i]
    /\ pendingReq' = pendingReq \cup {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admission, reserved, placed>>

AcquireAdmission(i) ==
    /\ i \in pendingReq
    /\ admission = NoneI
    /\ admission' = i
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, placed, pendingReq>>

ReserveSlot(i) ==
    /\ admission = i
    /\ reserved[i] = {}
    /\ \E s \in LocalSlots \ placed[i] :
         reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admission, placed, pendingReq>>

CommitPlacement(i) ==
    /\ admission = i
    /\ reserved[i] # {}
    /\ Cardinality(AllPlaced) < MaxCapacity
    /\ \E s \in reserved[i] :
         placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
    /\ pendingReq' = pendingReq \ {i}
    /\ admission' = NoneI

AbandonReservation(i) ==
    /\ admission = i
    /\ reserved[i] # {}
    /\ Cardinality(AllPlaced) >= MaxCapacity
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
    /\ admission' = NoneI
    /\ UNCHANGED <<placed, pendingReq>>

DepartContainer(i) ==
    \E s \in placed[i] :
        /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![i] = @ \ {s}]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<admission, reserved, pendingReq>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Request(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AcquireAdmission(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : ReserveSlot(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CommitPlacement(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AbandonReservation(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : DepartContainer(i)

vars == <<admission, reserved, placed, pendingReq>>

Fairness ==
    \A i \in Instances :
        /\ WF_vars(Request(i))
        /\ SF_vars(AcquireAdmission(i))
        /\ WF_vars(ReserveSlot(i))
        /\ WF_vars(CommitPlacement(i))
        /\ WF_vars(AbandonReservation(i))
        /\ WF_vars(DepartContainer(i))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the shared pool's bound is never exceeded by the two instances combined.
BoundedSharedCapacity == Cardinality(AllPlaced) <= MaxCapacity

AllRequestsEventuallySatisfied == \A i \in Instances : (i \in pendingReq) ~> (i \notin pendingReq)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {north, south}
    LocalSlots = {s1, s2}
    MaxCapacity = 3
    NoneI = none
INVARIANT BoundedSharedCapacity
PROPERTY AllRequestsEventuallySatisfied
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship terminal operates two independent crane-yard control instances (a north-side crane team and a south-side crane team) that share one physical container-storage pool of bounded capacity. Each instance manages its own local numbering of storage slots, but every container either instance places ultimately occupies space in the same shared pool, so the two instances must coordinate before adding anything. Admission into the pool follows a two-level, hierarchical scheme that mirrors coarse-then-fine locking: an instance must first hold the single, pool-wide admission permit (the coarse level, held by at most one instance at a time) before it is allowed to make a fine-grained reservation of one of its own local slots and then actually commit a container into the shared pool. Only after committing (or abandoning) its reservation does an instance give the pool-wide permit back up, letting the other instance proceed.

The full set of actions is:
1. Request: an instance with an idle local slot registers that it wants to place a new container in the shared pool.
2. AcquireAdmission: an instance with an outstanding request takes the pool-wide admission permit, provided no other instance currently holds it.
3. ReserveSlot: while holding the pool-wide permit, an instance picks one of its own not-yet-placed local slots and marks it as its fine-grained in-progress reservation.
4. CommitPlacement: while holding the permit with an in-progress reservation, if the shared pool's combined occupancy (counted across both instances) is below the bound, the instance commits its reserved slot's container into the shared pool, clears its request and reservation, and gives the pool-wide permit back.
5. AbandonReservation: while holding the permit with an in-progress reservation, if the shared pool is already at its bound (so the commit cannot proceed), the instance drops the reservation and gives the pool-wide permit back so the other instance is not starved; its request stays outstanding to retry later.
6. DepartContainer: any instance may remove one of its own already-committed containers from the shared pool at any time, freeing a unit of shared capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the total number of containers committed into the shared pool across both crane-yard instances together never exceeds the pool's fixed bound.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every outstanding placement request, from either instance, is eventually satisfied (its container is committed into the shared pool), even though the two instances contend for the single pool-wide admission permit and the shared pool can transiently be full.

---- MODULE W4Od7m9p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Y1, Y2, Total, MaxEpoch

\* Two crane-yard control zones (Y1, Y2) share one equipment pool. A global
\* reconfiguration epoch fences which zone may touch the pool: a zone whose
\* local epoch lags the global epoch is "stale" and must re-sync before it
\* may check out or return equipment; dispatch may force-recall a stale
\* zone's equipment so nothing is ever stranded across a reconfiguration.

Yards == {Y1, Y2}

VARIABLES epoch, yardEpoch, held, poolFree

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ yardEpoch \in [Yards -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ held \in [Yards -> 0..Total]
  /\ poolFree \in 0..Total

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ yardEpoch = [y \in Yards |-> 0]
  /\ held = [y \in Yards |-> 0]
  /\ poolFree = Total

Checkout(y) ==
  /\ yardEpoch[y] = epoch
  /\ poolFree > 0
  /\ poolFree' = poolFree - 1
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![y] = held[y] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, yardEpoch>>

Return(y) ==
  /\ yardEpoch[y] = epoch
  /\ held[y] > 0
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![y] = held[y] - 1]
  /\ poolFree' = poolFree + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, yardEpoch>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardEpoch, held, poolFree>>

Sync(y) ==
  /\ yardEpoch[y] < epoch
  /\ yardEpoch' = [yardEpoch EXCEPT ![y] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, held, poolFree>>

Recall(y) ==
  /\ yardEpoch[y] < epoch
  /\ held[y] > 0
  /\ poolFree' = poolFree + held[y]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![y] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, yardEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ (\E y \in Yards : Checkout(y))
  \/ (\E y \in Yards : Return(y))
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ (\E y \in Yards : Sync(y))
  \/ (\E y \in Yards : Recall(y))

vars == <<epoch, yardEpoch, held, poolFree>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: total equipment across the shared pool and both zones' held
\* counts is fixed -- reconfiguration and recall only move units around,
\* they never create or destroy them.
Conservation == poolFree + held[Y1] + held[Y2] = Total

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Y1 = y1
    Y2 = y2
    Total = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2
INVARIANT Conservation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A container terminal operates two independently managed crane-yard control zones, Y1 and Y2, that both draw their mobile lifting units (reach-stacker equipment tokens) from one shared equipment pool operated by the terminal's central dispatch. The terminal's dispatch protocol is governed by a global reconfiguration epoch number. Whenever dispatch issues a reconfiguration (bumping the epoch), every zone's local view of the epoch immediately becomes stale until that zone explicitly re-synchronizes to the new epoch; a zone that has not yet re-synchronized may not check out or return equipment, since its authorization to touch the shared pool is fenced by the epoch it last synced to. Instead, dispatch may forcibly recall all equipment currently held by a stale (not-yet-resynchronized) zone straight back into the shared pool, without that zone's cooperation, to guarantee equipment is never stranded across a reconfiguration boundary. The full set of actions is: a zone that is synced to the current epoch checking out one free unit from the shared pool into its own held count; a zone that is synced to the current epoch returning one of its held units back into the shared pool; dispatch bumping the global epoch (a reconfiguration event, up to a fixed maximum number of reconfigurations); a stale zone re-synchronizing its local epoch to the current global epoch; and dispatch recalling all of a stale zone's held equipment back into the shared pool in one step. No action ever manufactures a new equipment unit or scraps an existing one -- every unit is always either sitting free in the shared pool or checked out and held by exactly one of the two zones. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of units free in the shared pool plus the number of units held by zone Y1 plus the number of units held by zone Y2 equals the fixed total number of equipment units the terminal owns.

---- MODULE W4Od8m1p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS N, InitToken, Admin, MaxOverrides

\* A token circulates around a fixed ring of N registration nodes (numbered
\* 1..N, successor wraps around); only the current token holder may take
\* exclusive access to the shared seat ledger. A privileged admin may
\* bypass the ring entirely, seizing the ledger while it is idle, up to a
\* fixed override budget. The invariant protects exclusive access to the
\* ledger no matter who holds it.

Nodes == 1..N
Succ(n) == IF n = N THEN 1 ELSE n + 1

VARIABLES tokenAt, inCS, override, wantCS, overrideCount

TypeOK ==
  /\ tokenAt \in Nodes
  /\ inCS \subseteq (Nodes \cup {Admin})
  /\ override \in BOOLEAN
  /\ wantCS \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ overrideCount \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
  /\ tokenAt = InitToken
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ override = FALSE
  /\ wantCS = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
  /\ overrideCount = 0

Request(n) ==
  /\ ~wantCS[n]
  /\ wantCS' = [wantCS EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, inCS, override, overrideCount>>

PassToken ==
  /\ ~override
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ ~wantCS[tokenAt]
  /\ tokenAt' = Succ(tokenAt)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, override, wantCS, overrideCount>>

EnterCS(n) ==
  /\ ~override
  /\ tokenAt = n
  /\ wantCS[n]
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ inCS' = {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, override, wantCS, overrideCount>>

ExitCS(n) ==
  /\ n \in inCS
  /\ inCS' = {}
  /\ wantCS' = [wantCS EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ tokenAt' = Succ(n)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<override, overrideCount>>

AdminSeizeAndEnter ==
  /\ ~override
  /\ inCS = {}
  /\ overrideCount < MaxOverrides
  /\ override' = TRUE
  /\ inCS' = {Admin}
  /\ overrideCount' = overrideCount + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, wantCS>>

AdminExitAndRelease ==
  /\ Admin \in inCS
  /\ inCS' = {}
  /\ override' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenAt, wantCS, overrideCount>>

Next ==
  \/ (\E n \in Nodes : Request(n))
  \/ PassToken
  \/ (\E n \in Nodes : EnterCS(n))
  \/ (\E n \in Nodes : ExitCS(n))
  \/ AdminSeizeAndEnter
  \/ AdminExitAndRelease

vars == <<tokenAt, inCS, override, wantCS, overrideCount>>

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ \A n \in Nodes : WF_vars(EnterCS(n))
  /\ \A n \in Nodes : WF_vars(ExitCS(n))
  /\ WF_vars(AdminExitAndRelease)

\* Safety: at most one ring node or the admin ever holds the ledger.
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(inCS) <= 1

EventuallyServed == \A n \in Nodes : (wantCS[n] ~> (n \in inCS))

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    InitToken = 1
    Admin = admin
    MaxOverrides = 1
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY EventuallyServed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A university's course-registration system lets a small ring of registration-service nodes take turns writing to a single shared critical resource: the seat ledger for a capacity-limited course section. Exclusive access to the seat ledger is granted by a token that circulates around the ring in a fixed order; a node may write to the ledger only while it holds the token, and it must hold the token alone -- no other ring node or the administrator may touch the ledger at the same time. Each ring node independently decides, at any point, that it wants to update the ledger (for example, to enroll or drop a student); once it wants access it keeps wanting it until it is actually granted the resource. A node holding the token that does not currently want the resource simply passes the token on to the next node in the ring instead of using it. Separately, the registrar's office has a privileged administrator that can override the ring entirely: whenever the ledger is idle (no ring node and no prior admin session is using it) and the office has not yet exhausted its fixed budget of override sessions, the administrator may seize exclusive control of the ledger directly, bypassing the token protocol, make its correction, and later release control, after which the ring resumes circulating the token as before. The full set of actions is: a ring node deciding it wants ledger access; the token holder passing the token to the next node in the ring when it does not want access; the token holder entering the ledger (taking exclusive access) when it does want access; a node that holds exclusive access releasing it, clearing its own want-flag, and passing the token on to the next node in the ring so no single node can monopolize it by immediately re-requesting; the administrator seizing exclusive access of an idle ledger (consuming one unit of its override budget); and the administrator releasing the exclusive access it seized. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one participant -- whether a ring node or the administrator -- holds exclusive access to the seat ledger at a time. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every ring node that starts wanting access to the seat ledger eventually is granted exclusive access to it, even though the administrator may repeatedly interrupt the ring with override sessions in the meantime.

---- MODULE W4Od8m5p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Replicas, Capacity, Quorum

\* A university course-registration system replicates one course's roster
\* across several registrar replicas for fault tolerance. Every enroll/drop
\* action is first proposed, then voted on by replicas (each replica checks
\* the action against its OWN local, possibly-stale copy of the roster), and
\* only takes effect once a quorum of replicas has endorsed it -- at which
\* point the coordinator re-validates against the true authoritative roster
\* before committing. Sync messages that propagate a commit out to each
\* replica's local copy can be reordered/delivered out of turn, so a
\* replica's local view may transiently look inconsistent, but the
\* authoritative roster (the thing that actually holds a seat) is the only
\* thing the safety property protects.

VARIABLES enrolled, pending, voteMsgs, localView, syncMsgs

TypeOK ==
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Students
    /\ pending \subseteq [student: Students, kind: {"enroll", "drop"}]
    /\ voteMsgs \subseteq [replica: Replicas, student: Students, kind: {"enroll", "drop"}]
    /\ localView \in [Replicas -> SUBSET Students]
    /\ syncMsgs \subseteq [replica: Replicas, student: Students, kind: {"add", "remove"}]

Init ==
    /\ enrolled = {}
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ voteMsgs = {}
    /\ localView = [r \in Replicas |-> {}]
    /\ syncMsgs = {}

\* A student's enroll or drop is proposed, if it is currently sensible
\* against the true roster (can't propose to enroll someone already in,
\* can't propose to drop someone not in).
Propose(s, k) ==
    /\ [student |-> s, kind |-> k] \notin pending
    /\ (k = "enroll" => s \notin enrolled)
    /\ (k = "drop" => s \in enrolled)
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[student |-> s, kind |-> k]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, voteMsgs, localView, syncMsgs>>

\* A replica endorses a pending action using only its own local roster copy:
\* it always endorses a drop, but only endorses an enroll it believes there
\* is room for -- its local copy may be stale, so this is a heuristic, not
\* the authoritative check.
CastVote(r, s, k) ==
    /\ [student |-> s, kind |-> k] \in pending
    /\ [replica |-> r, student |-> s, kind |-> k] \notin voteMsgs
    /\ (k = "enroll" => Cardinality(localView[r]) < Capacity)
    /\ voteMsgs' = voteMsgs \cup {[replica |-> r, student |-> s, kind |-> k]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, pending, localView, syncMsgs>>

\* Once a quorum of replicas has endorsed an action, the coordinator commits
\* it -- but only after re-checking the action against the true authoritative
\* roster, which is what actually keeps capacity from ever being exceeded no
\* matter how stale the individual votes were. A commit also broadcasts a
\* sync diff to every replica.
Commit(s, k) ==
    LET diffKind == IF k = "enroll" THEN "add" ELSE "remove" IN
    /\ [student |-> s, kind |-> k] \in pending
    /\ Cardinality({r \in Replicas : [replica |-> r, student |-> s, kind |-> k] \in voteMsgs}) >= Quorum
    /\ (k = "enroll" => (s \notin enrolled /\ Cardinality(enrolled) < Capacity))
    /\ (k = "drop" => s \in enrolled)
    /\ enrolled' = IF k = "enroll" THEN enrolled \cup {s} ELSE enrolled \ {s}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {[student |-> s, kind |-> k]}
    /\ voteMsgs' = {m \in voteMsgs : m.student # s}
    /\ syncMsgs' = syncMsgs \cup {[replica |-> r, student |-> s, kind |-> diffKind] : r \in Replicas}
    /\ UNCHANGED localView

\* A replica applies one pending sync diff to its local copy. The network
\* can deliver these out of order, so a replica may apply a later commit's
\* diff before an earlier one's, leaving its local view transiently
\* inconsistent with the true commit order (though never with the true
\* roster's authoritative membership once fully caught up).
ApplySync(r, s, k) ==
    /\ [replica |-> r, student |-> s, kind |-> k] \in syncMsgs
    /\ localView' = [localView EXCEPT ![r] = IF k = "add" THEN @ \cup {s} ELSE @ \ {s}]
    /\ syncMsgs' = syncMsgs \ {[replica |-> r, student |-> s, kind |-> k]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, pending, voteMsgs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students, k \in {"enroll", "drop"} : Propose(s, k)
    \/ \E r \in Replicas, s \in Students, k \in {"enroll", "drop"} : CastVote(r, s, k)
    \/ \E s \in Students, k \in {"enroll", "drop"} : Commit(s, k)
    \/ \E r \in Replicas, s \in Students, k \in {"add", "remove"} : ApplySync(r, s, k)

vars == <<enrolled, pending, voteMsgs, localView, syncMsgs>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounds the amount of simultaneously in-flight coordination bookkeeping so
\* the reachable state space stays finite and small for model checking; it
\* does not restrict which actions are semantically allowed.
StateSpaceBound == Cardinality(pending) + Cardinality(voteMsgs) + Cardinality(syncMsgs) <= 5

\* The one thing that actually matters operationally: the authoritative,
\* quorum-committed roster never holds more students than the course has
\* seats for, regardless of how stale or reordered any replica's own view
\* of the roster becomes in the meantime.
CapacityRespected == Cardinality(enrolled) <= Capacity

nl:
A university's course-registration system replicates the roster for one popular, capacity-limited course across a small cluster of registrar replicas for fault tolerance. Every change to the roster -- enrolling a student or dropping a student -- is first proposed, then voted on by the replicas, and only takes effect once a quorum of replicas has endorsed it. Each replica endorses a proposal by consulting only its own local copy of the roster, which is kept up to date by sync messages that can be reordered or delivered out of turn, so a replica's local copy may lag behind or apply changes in a different order than they actually happened. To guard against this staleness, the coordinator that ultimately commits an action always re-checks it against the true, authoritative roster (not any one replica's local copy) before applying it.

The full set of actions is:
1. Propose: a student's enrollment or drop is proposed, as long as it is currently sensible against the true roster (you can't propose to enroll someone already enrolled, and you can't propose to drop someone not currently enrolled).
2. CastVote: a replica endorses a pending proposal using only its own local roster copy -- it always endorses a drop, but only endorses an enrollment if its own (possibly stale) local copy believes there is still room.
3. Commit: once a quorum of replicas has endorsed a pending proposal, the coordinator commits it, but only after re-validating the proposal against the true authoritative roster (rejecting it if, in truth, the course is already full or the student's true membership no longer matches what was proposed). A successful commit updates the true roster and broadcasts a sync message to every replica.
4. ApplySync: a replica applies one pending sync message to its own local roster copy. Because the network can reorder these messages, a replica may apply a later change before an earlier one, so its local copy can transiently disagree with the true commit order.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the true, authoritative course roster never holds more students than the course has seats for, no matter how stale or out-of-order any individual replica's local view of the roster becomes.
